11.17.1. Routes
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/urls.py: the application’s paths. Their protection is not documented here,
# but in security/acces.py (one rule per URL prefix).
# =========================================================================

from django.urls import path, re_path

from .vues import agenda, auth, espace, inscription, langue
from .vues.personnes import clients, medecins

urlpatterns = [
     # Login
    path("", auth.accueil, name="accueil"),
    path("login", auth.login, name="login"),
    path("logout", auth.logout, name="logout"),
     # language: fr or en only
    re_path(r"^langue/(?P<code>fr|en)$", langue.changer, name="langue"),
     # the calendar
    path("agenda", agenda.afficher, name="agenda"),
    path("agenda/reserver", agenda.reserver, name="agenda_reserver"),
    path("agenda/annuler", agenda.annuler, name="agenda_annuler"),
     # Create a customer account
    path("inscription/acces", inscription.acces, name="inscription_acces"),
    path("inscription", inscription.inscription, name="inscription"),
     # the patient portal
    path("mon-espace", espace.espace, name="espace"),
    path("mon-espace/annuler", espace.annuler_rv, name="espace_annuler"),
    path("mon-compte", espace.compte, name="compte"),
    path("mon-compte/supprimer", espace.supprimer_compte, name="compte_supprimer"),
     # Managing doctors and clients: paths created by both
     # objects GestionPersonnes; * "unpacks" the list they return
    *medecins.urls(),
    *clients.urls(),
]

The application’s routes, mounted at the root of the site by [config/urls.py]. The routes for managing doctors and clients are generated by two objects (discussed later); [*liste] places the elements of one list into another list (lines 32–33). The command [show_urls] does not exist in [Django] (it comes from an extension); a short script, launched by [python manage.py shell], lists them all, along with their names:

$ python manage.py shell -v 0 -c "from django.urls import get_resolver; [print(f'{str(p.pattern):32} {p.name}') for p in get_resolver().url_patterns[0].url_patterns]"
                                 accueil
login                            login
logout                           logout
^langue/(?P<code>fr|en)$         langue
agenda                           agenda
agenda/reserver                  agenda_reserver
agenda/annuler                   agenda_annuler
inscription/acces                inscription_acces
inscription                      inscription
mon-espace                       espace
mon-espace/annuler               espace_annuler
mon-compte                       compte
mon-compte/supprimer             compte_supprimer
medecins                         medecins_liste
medecins/ajouter                 medecins_ajout
medecins/<int:id>/modifier       medecins_modification
medecins/<int:id>/supprimer      medecins_supprimer
clients                          clients_liste
clients/ajouter                  clients_ajout
clients/<int:id>/modifier        clients_modification
clients/<int:id>/supprimer       clients_supprimer

The URL files are those from other versions of the application: they do not have a trailing slash ([/agenda], not [/agenda/]), and editing and deleting a doctor are POST requests ([/medecins/{id}/modifier], [/medecins/{id}/supprimer]), not PUT and DELETE as in Example 28. The code always generates the URL codes based on the street names ([redirect("login")], [reverse("agenda")], [{% url 'agenda' %}] in the templates, Example 04): changing a URL requires modifying only its route.

The methods accepted by each route are declared by the [require_GET], [require_POST], and [require_http_methods] decorators in the views (example 02). Access rules are not in the views, but in the [securite/acces.py] file, as seen above: one rule per URL prefix ([^/(medecins|clients)] for the administrator, [^/mon-] for patients...), and a final rule requiring an authenticated user for all other URL files. The URL URLs in the application were chosen for this purpose: all pages within the same role begin the same way.

docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/erreurs.py: the error page (400, 403, 404, 405, 419, 500), and the views
# that Django calls for errors it detects itself (see config/urls.py:
# handler400, handler403, handler404, handler500, and the setting CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW).
# =========================================================================

from django.shortcuts import render
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _

# the message for each code
MESSAGES = {
    400: _("La requête est invalide."),
    403: _("Votre rôle ne vous permet pas d'accéder à cette page."),
    404: _("Cette page n'existe pas."),
    405: _("Cette page n'existe pas."),
    419: _("La page a expiré : rechargez-la, puis recommencez."),
    500: _("Une erreur inattendue s'est produite. Réessayez plus tard."),
}


def page_erreur(request, code: int):
    return render(request, "erreur.html", {
        "titre_page": _("Erreur"), "code": code, "message": MESSAGES.get(code, MESSAGES[500]),
    }, status=code)


# the views where errors were detected by Django (exception: the exception that caused
# the error; view 500 does not receive it)
def erreur_400(request, exception):
    return page_erreur(request, 400)


def erreur_403(request, exception):
    return page_erreur(request, 403)


def erreur_404(request, exception):
    return page_erreur(request, 404)


def erreur_500(request):
    return page_erreur(request, 500)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# a missing or invalid anti-CSRF token: the page was likely displayed
# a long time ago, in another tab, before the token cookie was updated... Error
# 419, the (unofficial but widely used) code for an expired page. reason: the reason
# for the rejection, provided by CsrfViewMiddleware (in English)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
def csrf_refuse(request, reason=""):
    return page_erreur(request, 419)

The error page and the error views that [Django] detects itself:

  • lines 11–18: the message for each code. Code 405 is displayed as a “page not found” error;
  • lines 21–24: the error page, template [erreur.html], with response code HTTP ([status=code]). An unknown code receives the 500 error message ([dict.get(clé, défaut)]);
  • lines 29–42: the four views [handler400]... [handler500], referred to as [config/urls.py] (example 24). Their signature is determined by [Django]: the request and the exception that caused the error (except for error 500);
  • lines 51–52: a missing or invalid anti-CSRF token. The [CsrfViewMiddleware] middleware rejects the request before calling the view (Example 21), and instead calls the view associated with the [CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW] setting (see [config/settings.py]): the 419 error page, the (unofficial but widely used) code for an expired page. This occurs when a page has remained open in a tab for a long time, even though the token cookie has since changed. The page then displays: “The page has expired: reload it, then try again.” Its parameter [reason] is the reason for the rejection, in English, intended for the log rather than the user.

docs.title: 11.17.3. web/views/langue.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/langue.py: GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two buttons FR / EN in
# the navigation bar. Public route: it must be possible to change the language before
# logging in.
#
# The selection is stored in a cookie: with each subsequent request, the middleware
# FixerLangue reads it and sets the language for the request. Then you return to the page
# from which the user came (see Example 22).
# =========================================================================

from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from django.conf import settings
from django.shortcuts import redirect
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET


# code: fr or en (see web/urls.py: /language/de returns a 404 page)
@require_GET
def changer(request, code):
    reponse = redirect(page_d_origine(request))
    reponse.set_cookie(settings.LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME, code, max_age=365 * 24 * 3600,
                       secure=settings.COOKIE_SECURE, httponly=True, samesite="Lax")
    return reponse


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the previous page, based on the "Referer" header HTTP sent by the browser. We
# only retain the path and parameters (/agenda?...): redirect to a
# the full address provided by the request would allow the user to be sent to
# another site (a vulnerability known as an “open redirect”). urlsplit splits a URL into its
# components: scheme (http), netloc (the machine), path, query...
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
def page_d_origine(request) -> str:
    referer = urlsplit(request.headers.get("Referer", ""))
    chemin = referer.path
     # "//site.com/..." would be interpreted by the browser as an address on a
     # AUTRE site: also rejected
    if not referer.scheme or not chemin.startswith("/") or chemin.startswith("//") \
            or chemin.startswith("/langue/"):
        return "/"
    return f"{chemin}?{referer.query}" if referer.query else chemin

The FR / EN buttons on the navigation bar: the language selection is stored in a cookie for one year (example 22), after which the browser returns to the page it came from. The cookie is [HttpOnly]: the [JavaScript] on the page does not need to read it. It is not signed: the [FixerLangue] middleware verifies its value, and an unknown value results in French (see the chapter on scopes).

  • Line 20: [code] is equivalent to [fr] or [en]: the route (a regular expression, [re_path], example 02) accepts only these two values. [/langue/de] does not match any route (404 page);
  • lines 34–42: The previous page is specified by the header HTTP [Referer] that the browser sends with the request. This data is provided by the client and is therefore suspect: redirecting to a full URL from the request would allow an attacker to send the user to their own site via a link to [/langue/fr] with a fake [Referer] (the so-called “open redirect” vulnerability). Therefore, we retain only the path and parameters ([/agenda?idMedecin=1&...]), extracted by the [urlsplit] function from the standard library, which splits a URL into its parts ([scheme], [netloc], [path], [query]...). A path that begins with [//] is also rejected: a browser interprets [//site.com/page] as an address on another site. Finally, you cannot return to [/langue/...]: a loop. A backslash ([\]) at the end of a line ([Python]) extends the instruction to the next line.
$ curl -si http://localhost:8000/language/en -H "Referer: http://localhost:8000/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-09-30"
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: /agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-09-30
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_langue=en; expires=Mon, 27 Sep 2027 17:56:57 GMT; HttpOnly; Max-Age=31536000; Path=/; SameSite=Lax
...
$ curl -si http://localhost:8000/language/en -H "Referer: https://pirate.com//page"
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: /
...

docs.title: 11.17.4. web/views/auth.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/auth.py: the PUBLIQUES routes for the connection:
#    GE T         / redirects to the role's home page (or to /login)
#    GE T /log  in displays the login form (with its CAPTCHA)
#    POST /logi  n checks attempt limit, CAPTCHA, username/password
#    POST /logou t logs out
#
# Protection against bots, in this order:
#    1. Too many recent failed attempts for this login from this address IP?
#       -> immediate rejection, without even checking the password;
#    2. Incorrect CAPTCHA answer? -> Denied (counted as a failed attempt);
#    3. Only then is the password verified.
# The password for an attempt rejected in steps 1 or 2 is not verified:
# A bot therefore cannot learn anything by persisting.
# =========================================================================

from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_http_methods, require_POST

from modeles.models import Role
from securite import auth, captchas, limiteur

from .. import outils


# The home page for each role, immediately after logging in: the name of its route
def page_accueil(role: str) -> str:
    return "espace" if role == Role.USER else "agenda"


# GET /: the route is public; the user, if there is one, is known
@require_GET
def accueil(request):
    if request.utilisateur is not None:
        return redirect(page_accueil(request.utilisateur.role))
    return redirect("login")


# GET /login[?login=xxx]: the form; the optional parameter pre-fills the
# login field (used immediately after creating an account; see vues/inscription.py).
# POST /login: login
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
def login(request):
    if request.method == "POST":
        return connexion(request)
     # already logged in (token still valid): goes directly to the home page
    if request.utilisateur is not None:
        return redirect(page_accueil(request.utilisateur.role))
     # [:30]: 30 characters maximum
    return page(request, request.GET.get("login", "")[:30], None)


def connexion(request):
    login = request.POST.get("login", "")
    password = request.POST.get("password", "")
    ip = outils.ip(request)
     # 1. Too many recent failed attempts? ngettext: singular or plural, depending on the number
    minutes = limiteur.minutes_blocage_login(ip, login)
    if minutes > 0:
        return page(request, login, ngettext(
            "Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minute.",
            "Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minutes.",
            minutes) % {"minutes": minutes})
     # 2. the CAPTCHA
    if not captchas.verifier(request.POST.get("captcha_id", ""), request.POST.get("captcha", "")):
        limiteur.echec_login(ip, login)
        return page(request, login, _("Les caractères recopiés ne correspondent pas à l'image. "
                                      "Une nouvelle image vous est proposée."))
     # 3. the password
    user = auth.valider(login, password) if login and password else None
    if user is None:
        limiteur.echec_login(ip, login)
        return page(request, login, _("Login ou mot de passe incorrect."))
    limiteur.reussite_login(ip, login)
    return auth.poser_jeton(redirect(page_accueil(user.role)), user)


# POST /logout: Clear the token cookie, then go to the login page.
# POST only: a simple link (GET), placed on another site, cannot
# log the user out without their knowledge
@require_POST
def logout(request):
    return auth.effacer_jeton(redirect("login"))


# the form, always with a NOUVEAU CAPTCHA (each image is used only once
# time); the entered username is displayed again, but never the password. An error: the
# 422 error code, as if the form were invalid (see example 19)
def page(request, login: str, erreur: str | None):
    return render(request, "login.html", {
        "titre_page": _("Connexion"), "erreur": erreur, "login": login,
        "captcha": captchas.generer(),
    }, status=422 if erreur else 200)

The connection, which follows Example 27:

  • lines 28–29: the home page for each role, along with its route name: “My Space” for a patient, and the calendar for others;
  • lines 33–37: the address [/] redirects to the role’s home page or to the login page. The route is public (securite/acces.py): [request.utilisateur] is the user established by the middleware [Authentification], if there is one;
  • lines 43–51: A user who is already logged in is taken directly to their home page. The optional parameter [login] of URL pre-fills the field (after an account is created); [[:30]] truncates it to 30 characters;
  • lines 54–76: the login process, in the order shown in Example 27: potential blocking, the CAPTCHA, the password (the anti-CSRF token has already been verified by the middleware). A password is never verified for an attempt rejected by the limiter or the CAPTCHA: a bot learns nothing by persisting. [ngettext(singulier, pluriel, nombre)] (lines 61–64) selects the appropriate format for the number in the language of the request (Example 22); the parameter [%(minutes)d] is set after translation. If the attempt fails, the page is rendered directly (no redirection): the re-displayed form always has a new CAPTCHA and the entered login. If successful, the login counter is reset to zero, and the browser is redirected to the role’s home page with the token cookie;
  • lines 82–84: Logout deletes the token cookie (Example 25). It only accepts POST, along with the anti-CSRF token: a simple link placed on another site cannot log the user out without their knowledge;
  • lines 90–94: the login page. An error is returned with code 422 (Unprocessable Content), such as an invalid form (example 19).

The login page receives the variable [titre_page], the page title, which has already been translated: all views provide this to their template for the [<title>] tag and the page title (see below).

docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/vues/agenda.py: the calendar page: selecting a doctor and a day,
# this doctor’s schedule for that day, booking and canceling appointments.
#
#    GE T /schedule?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09             -23 the page
#    GE T /schedule?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23&book=7     the same page, with the
#                                                           booking window
#                                                           for time slot 7 is open
#    POST /calendar/book                                   creates an appointment
#    POST /calendar/canc                                  el cancels an appointment
#
# The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, add it to
# bookmark, or use the browser’s “Back” button—without a single line of
# JavaScript.
#
# What everyone sees and can do:
#
#    | rol         e | displayed re           served slot           | Reserve | Cancel |
#   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
#    | ADMIN, DOCTOR | patient name                         | for     a patient | yes |
#                  |                                    |            | selected from list | |
#    | USER (patient)| “Reserved,” or SON name if it i s | for himself, if he| no (*) |
#                  | | his own            appointment          | does not already have an appointment| |
#                  |                                                         | | upcoming | |
#
#    (*) The patient cancels their appointment from their "My Account" page.
#
# CONFIDENTIALITÉ: For a patient, the names of the AUTRES patients are not
# simply hidden by the template—it is never sent to the template. The HTML
# sent to the browser therefore does not contain it, even if hidden (a simple "View
# source code" would reveal it otherwise).
#
# No past reservations: the “Reserve” button appears only for
# today and the following days (and the business layer would reject it outright
# case).
#
# Security: All URL /calendar operations require an authenticated user, and
# /calendar/cancel the role ADMIN or DOCTOR (see security/acces.py).
# =========================================================================

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from urllib.parse import urlencode

from django.contrib import messages
from django.core.exceptions import BadRequest
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_POST

from domaine.agenda import AgendaMedecinJour
from metier import erreurs
from metier.dates import aujourdhui
from metier.erreurs import MetierErreur
from modeles.models import Client, Personne, Role

from .. import outils
from ..application import application
from ..modeles_vues import AgendaVue, LigneAgenda, OptionVue, ReservationVue


# who is logged in, and what actions are they authorized to perform on this page?
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Droits:
    gestionnaire: bool                 # ADMIN or DOCTOR
    patient: Client | None             # the logged-in client (role USER), otherwise None
    patient_peut_reserver: bool        # a USER with no upcoming appointments


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /calendar
# The parameters of the URL are read in raw format (request.GET), to distinguish a
# ABSENT (None) parameter from a VIDE (?idMedecin=) parameter.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_GET
def afficher(request):
    erreur = None
    utilisateur = outils.utilisateur(request)
    droits = calculer_droits(request)
    app = application()
     # the day: that of the URL if valid, otherwise today
    jour = aujourdhui()
    jour_brut = request.GET.get("jour")
    if jour_brut is not None:
        jour_demande = outils.date_valide(jour_brut)
        if jour_demande is not None:
            jour = jour_demande
        else:
            erreur = _("La date demandée n'est pas valide.")
    jour_reservable = jour >= aujourdhui()
     # the doctor: the one from URL; otherwise, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves
    id_medecin_brut = request.GET.get("idMedecin")
    id_medecin = outils.entier_positif(id_medecin_brut)
    if id_medecin_brut is None and utilisateur.role == Role.DOCTOR:
        medecin = app.get_medecin_by_user_id(utilisateur.user_id)
        id_medecin = medecin.id if medecin else None
     # the drop-down list of doctors
    medecins = [option(m, m.id == id_medecin) for m in app.get_all_medecins()]
     # the calendar, if a doctor is selected (and the date is valid)
    agenda = None
    if id_medecin is not None and erreur is None:
        agenda_medecin = app.get_agenda_medecin_jour(id_medecin, jour)
        if agenda_medecin is None:
            erreur = _("Ce médecin n'existe pas (ou plus).")
        else:
            agenda = agenda_vue(agenda_medecin, droits, jour_reservable)
     # the booking window: only if the requested time slot is bookable by
     # this user
    reservation = None
    id_creneau = outils.entier_positif(request.GET.get("reserver"))
    if agenda is not None and id_creneau is not None:
        ligne = next((l for l in agenda.lignes if l.id_creneau == id_creneau and l.reservable), None)
        if ligne is not None:
            reservation = ReservationVue(
                ligne.id_creneau,
                ligne.horaire,
                [option(c, False) for c in app.get_all_clients()] if droits.gestionnaire else [],
                droits.patient.libelle() if droits.patient else None)
    return render(request, "agenda.html", {
        "titre_page": _("Agenda"),
        "erreur": erreur,
        "medecins": medecins,
        "id_medecin": id_medecin,
        "jour": outils.iso(jour),
        "agenda": agenda,
        "reservation": reservation,
         # the calendar displayed, without the booking window
        "url_retour": url_agenda(id_medecin, jour) if id_medecin is not None else reverse("agenda"),
        "info": info_patient(droits, agenda),
    })


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /calendar/book   fields: idMedecin, day, idCreneau, idClient
#
# For a patient (USER), the field idClient is IGNORÉ: the patient always makes reservations for
# themselves. Relying on a field sent by the browser would allow a
# malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name.
#
# "Post/Redirect/Get" pattern: regardless of the result, we do not generate a
# page here—we display a flash message and redirect to the calendar (see example 20).
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def reserver(request):
    id_medecin, jour = agenda_demande(request)
    id_creneau = outils.entier_positif(request.POST.get("idCreneau"))
    if id_medecin is None or id_creneau is None:
         # -> “Invalid Request” page (see web/middleware.py)
        raise BadRequest("agenda ou créneau invalide")
    app = application()
    utilisateur = outils.utilisateur(request)
    if utilisateur.est_patient:
        client = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    else:
        id_client = outils.entier_positif(request.POST.get("idClient"))
        if id_client is None:
             # No patient selected: the booking window reopens
            messages.error(request, _("Choisissez un patient."))
            return redirect(url_agenda(id_medecin, jour, id_creneau))
        client = app.get_client_by_id(id_client)
    creneau = app.get_creneau_by_id(id_creneau)
    if client is None:
        messages.error(request, _("Ce client n'existe pas (ou plus)."))
    elif creneau is None or creneau.medecin_id != id_medecin:
        messages.error(request, _("Ce créneau n'existe pas (ou plus)."))
    else:
        try:
             # the rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment per
             # patient, available time slot) are verified by the business layer
            app.ajouter_rv(jour, creneau, client)
            messages.success(request, _("Rendez-vous enregistré."))
        except MetierErreur as e:
             # same rule, but a message to the second person when the patient
             # the patient makes the appointment themselves (“You have already...” rather than “This patient...””).
             # Other exceptions (true errors) are not caught: 500 page
            if e.code == erreurs.PATIENT_A_UN_RV and utilisateur.est_patient:
                messages.error(request, _("Vous avez déjà un rendez-vous à venir : "
                                          "annulez-le pour en prendre un autre."))
            else:
                messages.error(request, e.message)
    return redirect(url_agenda(id_medecin, jour))


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /schedule/cancel   fields: idRv, idMedecin, day
# (a patient cancels SON an appointment from "My Account," not from here)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def annuler(request):
    id_medecin, jour = agenda_demande(request)
    id_rv = outils.entier_positif(request.POST.get("idRv"))
    if id_medecin is None or id_rv is None:
        raise BadRequest("agenda ou rendez-vous invalide")
    app = application()
    rv = app.get_rv_by_id(id_rv)
    if rv is None:
         # already canceled (by someone else, or by double-clicking)
        messages.error(request, _("Ce rendez-vous n'existe pas (ou plus)."))
    else:
        app.supprimer_rv(rv)
        messages.success(request, _("Rendez-vous annulé."))
    return redirect(url_agenda(id_medecin, jour))


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Who is logged in, and what are their permissions on this page?
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
def calculer_droits(request) -> Droits:
    if not outils.utilisateur(request).est_patient:
        return Droits(gestionnaire=True, patient=None, patient_peut_reserver=False)
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    rv_a_venir = application().get_rv_a_venir_client(patient.id)
     # not list: true for an empty list
    return Droits(gestionnaire=False, patient=patient, patient_peut_reserver=not rv_a_venir)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the doctor’s schedule, formatted for the template—and filtered according to permissions
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
def agenda_vue(agenda_medecin: AgendaMedecinJour, droits: Droits, jour_reservable: bool) -> AgendaVue:
    id_medecin = agenda_medecin.medecin.id
    jour = agenda_medecin.jour
    lignes = []
    for cmj in agenda_medecin.creneaux_medecin_jour:
        creneau = cmj.creneau
        rv = cmj.rv
        libre = rv is None
         # the logged-in patient’s appointment?
        moi = rv is not None and droits.patient is not None and rv.client_id == droits.patient.id
        lignes.append(LigneAgenda(
            id_creneau=creneau.id,
            horaire=creneau.horaire(),
            libre=libre,
             # LE privacy setting: a patient only sees the name from SON
             # appointment; for others, None (the template displays “Reserved”)
            patient=rv.client.libelle() if rv is not None and (droits.gestionnaire or moi) else None,
            moi=moi,
            reservable=libre and jour_reservable and (droits.gestionnaire or droits.patient_peut_reserver),
            url_reserver=url_agenda(id_medecin, jour, creneau.id),
            id_rv=rv.id if rv is not None and droits.gestionnaire else None))
    return AgendaVue(agenda_medecin.medecin.libelle(), outils.formater_jour(jour), lignes)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- Utility Functions
# hidden fields idMedecin / daily forms POST ; (None, None) if they are
# invalid
def agenda_demande(request) -> tuple[int | None, date | None]:
    id_medecin = outils.entier_positif(request.POST.get("idMedecin"))
    jour = outils.date_valide(request.POST.get("jour"))
    return (None, None) if id_medecin is None or jour is None else (id_medecin, jour)


# /calendar?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23[&reserver=7]: reverse-engineers the path to the
# route, URL-encodes the parameters of the URL, correctly encoded (see example 04)
def url_agenda(id_medecin: int, jour: date, reserver: int | None = None) -> str:
    parametres = {"idMedecin": id_medecin, "jour": outils.iso(jour)}
    if reserver is not None:
        parametres["reserver"] = reserver
    return f"{reverse('agenda')}?{urlencode(parametres)}"


def option(p: Personne, selectionne: bool) -> OptionVue:
    return OptionVue(p.id, p.libelle(), selectionne)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the informational message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment (which is why
# there is no “Book” button), or None. Not needed if SON the appointment appears
# in the displayed calendar (in blue): this is the case right after they have just
# scheduled, in which case the message would be moved
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
def info_patient(droits: Droits, agenda: AgendaVue | None) -> str | None:
    if droits.patient is None or droits.patient_peut_reserver:
        return None
    rv_affiche = agenda is not None and any(l.moi for l in agenda.lignes)
    return None if rv_affiche else _("Vous avez déjà un rendez-vous à venir : "
                                     "annulez-le pour en prendre un autre.")

The application’s main page. The header comment summarizes what each user sees and can do.

docs.title: 11.17.5.1. The URL elements of the page
docs.text: The entire page is described by its URL: [/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-09-30] displays Doctor 1’s schedule for that day; [&reserver=4] also opens the window for booking Slot 4. You can reload the page, bookmark it, or use the browser’s Back button without a single line of [JavaScript]. The form at the top of the page (for selecting the doctor and the day) is a GET form (example 17): it reloads the page with new parameters. The appointment booking window is opened by a simple link and closed by a link to the same page without the [reserver] parameter.

docs.title: 11.17.5.2. GET /calendar
docs.text:
Lines 76–131:

  • the parameters for URL are read as raw data ([request.GET.get("jour")]), without a form: a missing parameter ([None]) is not an error (it defaults to today or no doctor); an invalid date is an error, displayed at the bottom of the page (the doctor and day selections remain displayed, but not the calendar); a doctor or time slot number that is not a positive integer is simply ignored;
  • A logged-in user who has not selected a doctor sees their own schedule: the system searches for their doctor based on their account ([get_medecin_by_user_id]);
  • the drop-down list of doctors: a parsed list converts each doctor's name to [OptionVue];
  • the calendar, formatted and filtered according to the user’s permissions ([agenda_vue], below);
  • the booking window, only if the requested time slot is bookable by that user: a patient who attempts to generate the URL [&reserver=2] for a booked time slot would get nothing. [next(...)] returns the first line of the appropriate calendar, or [None]. The list of patients is provided only to the administrator and doctors; a patient sees only their own name;
  • the template receives its variables ([render], example 13), including [titre_page] and [erreur], which are read by the base template.

docs.title: 11.17.5.3. POST /agenda/reserve
docs.text:
Lines 144–182:

  • the hidden fields of the appointment form (doctor, day, time slot). Invalid; this can only be a manually created request: [BadRequest], the “invalid request” page (400), via the middleware [PageErreur];
  • For a patient, the field [idClient] is ignored: the patient always books for themselves ([outils.patient_connecte]). Trusting a field sent by the browser would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name. For the administrator and doctors, a patient must have been selected; otherwise, the reservation window reopens with a message;
  • the time slot must belong to the doctor on the page ([creneau.medecin_id]: the foreign key, without a query);
  • the business rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment, available time slot) are verified by the business logic layer. A [MetierErreur] becomes a flash error message. The same rejection, “one upcoming appointment,” is displayed to the second person on behalf of the patient themselves (“You already have…”). Any other exception is not intercepted: this is a true error (500 page);
  • in all cases, the Post/Redirect/Get pattern (example 20) applies: a pop-up message and a redirect to the calendar.

docs.title: 11.17.5.4. POST /calendar/cancel
docs.text: Lines 189–203: Cancellation of an appointment by the administrator or a doctor (rule [^/agenda/annuler$] derived from [securite/acces.py]). An appointment that no longer exists (already canceled by someone else, or due to a double-click) is not an error: it’s just a message.

docs.title: 11.17.5.5. Permissions, the formatted calendar, and utility functions
docs.text:
• lines 64–68 and 209–215: what the user is authorized to do on the page, within a data class: is the user an administrator (ADMIN or DOCTOR)? a patient (and which one)? Can this patient make a reservation (no upcoming appointments)? [not liste] is true for an empty list;
  • Lines 221–242: the doctor’s schedule, converted into rows for the template. The confidentiality issue is on line 237: a patient is shown only the name of their appointment. For the others, the attribute [patient] is set to [None], and the template displays “Reserved.” The name is not masked by the template: it is never transmitted to the template and therefore does not appear in the page’s source code, where it would be easy to read. The “Reserve” button is displayed for an available time slot on a future date to an administrator or a patient who can make a reservation; the “Cancel” button is displayed only to administrators. The named parameters ([id_creneau=creneau.id]) make the construction of an object with eight attributes readable;
  • lines 248–251: the hidden fields of the POST forms. The function returns a tuple, which the view unpacks into two variables ([id_medecin, jour = agenda_demande(request)], lines 146 and 191);
  • lines 256–260: the URL for a doctor’s schedule on a given day. [reverse("agenda")] returns the route path; [urlencode] generates the parameters, correctly encoded: [/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-09-30];
  • lines 273–278: the message explaining to a patient why there is no “Book” button (they already have an upcoming appointment), unless that appointment is in the displayed calendar (immediately after booking it, the message would be moved). [any(...)]: Does at least one line check the condition?

docs.title: 11.17.6. web/views/personnes.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/vues/personnes.py: doctor management and client management (reserved for
# the ADMIN) are IDENTIQUES: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than
# writing the same views twice, we write them once, like the MÉTHODES
# of a class, GestionPersonnes; two OBJETS from this class—doctors and
# clients, differ only in what sets them apart: the section name
# (doctors or clients), the texts, and the methods of the ApplicationModel to be called.
#
# A method of an object is called with the object (self): the view objet.liste(request)
# thus knows which section is being referenced. The urls() method generates the routes for
# the section:
#
#    GE T /doctor                  s                      list medecins_liste
#    GE T /doctors/add            empty fo          rm medecins_ajout
#    POST /doctors/add            cr                 eation medecins_ajout
#    GE T /doctors/{id}/edit      pre-filled form     medecins_modification
#    POST /doctors/{id}/edit      edit               medecins_modification
#    POST /doctors/{id}/delete     deletion                medecins_supprimer
#
# (and the same URL under /clients). The templates are also shared:
# templates/people/liste.html and people/formulaire.html.
#
# SÉCURITÉ: the rule ^/(doctors|clients) in security/acces.py reserves all these
# URL to ADMIN—including any that might be added later.
# =========================================================================

from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from django.contrib import messages
from django.http import Http404
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.urls import path, reverse
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_http_methods, require_POST

from metier import erreurs
from metier.erreurs import MetierErreur
from modeles.models import Personne

from ..application import application
from ..formulaires import PersonneForm

# the form fields affected by each business "data entry" error (a
# duplicate): these are highlighted in red, with the message at the bottom of the page
CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER = {
    erreurs.LOGIN_PRIS: ["login"],
    erreurs.MEDECIN_EXISTE_DEJA: ["prenom", "nom"],
    erreurs.CLIENT_EXISTE_DEJA: ["prenom", "nom"],
}


# the texts specific to each type of person; %(name)s, %(login)s: the
# message parameters
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Textes:
    titre: str                  # "Doctors"
    ajouter: str                # "Add a doctor"
    modifier: str               # "Edit a doctor"
    vide: str                   # "No doctors."
    confirmer_suppression: str  # "Delete this doctor...?"
    ajoute: str                 # "The doctor %(name)s has been added (login: %(login)s)."
    modifie: str
    supprime: str


class GestionPersonnes:
    def __init__(self, section: str, textes: Textes, lister: Callable, trouver: Callable,
                 creer: Callable, mettre_a_jour: Callable, effacer: Callable):
         # "doctors" or "clients": the start of the path and the names of the routes
        self.section = section
        self.textes = textes
         # the ApplicationModel methods to be called (functions; see below)
        self.lister = lister
        self.trouver = trouver
        self.creer = creer
        self.mettre_a_jour = mettre_a_jour
        self.effacer = effacer

     # the routes in the section; self.liste: the method associated with the CET object
    def urls(self):
        s = self.section
        return [
            path(f"{s}", require_GET(self.liste), name=f"{s}_liste"),
            path(f"{s}/ajouter", require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])(self.ajout), name=f"{s}_ajout"),
            path(f"{s}/<int:id>/modifier", require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])(self.modification),
                 name=f"{s}_modification"),
            path(f"{s}/<int:id>/supprimer", require_POST(self.supprimer), name=f"{s}_supprimer"),
        ]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # GET /doctors (or /clients)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def liste(self, request):
        return render(request, "personnes/liste.html", {
            "titre_page": self.textes.titre, "textes": self.textes, "section": self.section,
            "url_ajout": reverse(f"{self.section}_ajout"), "personnes": self.lister()})

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # GET /doctors/add: the empty form; POST: creation
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def ajout(self, request):
        if request.method == "GET":
            return self.page(request, PersonneForm(initial={"titre": "Mr"}), None)
        formulaire = PersonneForm(request.POST)
        if not formulaire.is_valid():
            return self.page(request, formulaire, None)
        try:
            personne = self.creer(formulaire.donnees())
        except MetierErreur as e:
            return self.erreur_metier(request, e, formulaire, None)
        messages.success(request, str(self.textes.ajoute) % parametres(personne))
        return redirect(f"{self.section}_liste")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # GET /doctors/{id}/edit: the pre-filled form; POST: the edit.
     # <int:id>: a parameter consisting of numbers (see example 02):
     # /doctors/abc/edit does not correspond to any route (404 page)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def modification(self, request, id):
        personne = self.trouver(id)
        if personne is None:
            raise Http404("personne inconnue")
        if request.method == "GET":
             # the form, pre-filled with the person’s values (the password
             # is never displayed)
            formulaire = PersonneForm(creation=False, initial={
                "titre": personne.titre, "prenom": personne.prenom, "nom": personne.nom,
                "login": personne.compte.login, "version": personne.version})
            return self.page(request, formulaire, personne)
        formulaire = PersonneForm(request.POST, creation=False)
        if not formulaire.is_valid():
            return self.page(request, formulaire, personne)
        try:
            personne = self.mettre_a_jour(id, formulaire.donnees())
        except MetierErreur as e:
            return self.erreur_metier(request, e, formulaire, personne)
        messages.success(request, str(self.textes.modifie) % parametres(personne))
        return redirect(f"{self.section}_liste")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # POST /doctors/{id}/delete (the confirmation "Are you sure?" is requested
     # before the form is submitted; see static/js/app.js)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def supprimer(self, request, id):
        personne = self.trouver(id)
        try:
            self.effacer(id)
            messages.success(request, str(self.textes.supprime) % parametres(personne))
        except MetierErreur as e:
            messages.error(request, e.message)
        return redirect(f"{self.section}_liste")

     # ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions
     # If the user is None: creation form; otherwise: update form.
     # A form was rejected (invalid input or business rule): code 422
    def page(self, request, formulaire, personne, erreur=None, champs_invalides=()):
        refuse = erreur is not None or (formulaire.is_bound and bool(formulaire.errors))
        titre = self.textes.ajouter if personne is None else self.textes.modifier
        return render(request, "personnes/formulaire.html", {
            "titre_page": titre,
            "formulaire": formulaire.signaler(champs_invalides),
            "erreur": erreur,
            "url_liste": reverse(f"{self.section}_liste"),
        }, status=422 if refuse else 200)

     # A business rule rejected the write operation: the form is redisplayed, with
     # the user’s input (without the password), the business layer message
     # business layer (at the bottom of the page), and the relevant fields, if any, highlighted in
     # red so the user can immediately see what to correct
    def erreur_metier(self, request, e: MetierErreur, formulaire, personne):
        if e.code in (erreurs.MEDECIN_INTROUVABLE, erreurs.CLIENT_INTROUVABLE):
             # which has since been removed by another ADMIN: return to the list
            messages.error(request, e.message)
            return redirect(f"{self.section}_liste")
        return self.page(request, formulaire, personne, e.message, CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.code, []))


# the %(name)s and %(login)s parameters in the "added / modified / deleted" messages
def parametres(personne: Personne | None) -> dict:
    if personne is None:
        return {"nom": "", "login": ""}
    return {"nom": f"{personne.prenom} {personne.nom}", "login": personne.compte.login}


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the two objects. lambda: a small anonymous function that calls the correct one
# method of ApplicationModel at the time of the request. The texts are translated
# "lazily" (gettext_lazy): when they are displayed, in the
# language of the request, rather than when the module is loaded
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

medecins = GestionPersonnes(
    "medecins",
    Textes(_("Médecins"), _("Ajouter un médecin"), _("Modifier un médecin"), _("Aucun médecin."),
           _("Supprimer ce médecin, ses créneaux horaires et son compte utilisateur ?"),
           _("Le médecin %(nom)s a été ajouté (login : %(login)s)."),
           _("Le médecin %(nom)s a été modifié."), _("Le médecin %(nom)s a été supprimé.")),
    lister=lambda: application().get_all_medecins(),
    trouver=lambda id: application().get_medecin_by_id(id),
    creer=lambda donnees: application().ajouter_medecin(donnees),
    mettre_a_jour=lambda id, donnees: application().modifier_medecin(id, donnees),
    effacer=lambda id: application().supprimer_medecin(id))

clients = GestionPersonnes(
    "clients",
    Textes(_("Clients"), _("Ajouter un client"), _("Modifier un client"), _("Aucun client."),
           _("Supprimer ce client, son compte utilisateur et tous ses rendez-vous ?"),
           _("Le client %(nom)s a été ajouté (login : %(login)s)."),
           _("Le client %(nom)s a été modifié."), _("Le client %(nom)s a été supprimé.")),
    lister=lambda: application().get_all_clients(),
    trouver=lambda id: application().get_client_by_id(id),
    creer=lambda donnees: application().ajouter_client(donnees),
    mettre_a_jour=lambda id, donnees: application().modifier_client(id, donnees),
    effacer=lambda id: application().supprimer_client(id))

The management of doctors and clients is identical: same list, same form, same rules. The views are written once, like the methods of a class, [GestionPersonnes]; two objects of this class, [medecins] and [clients], differ only in what sets them apart: the section name, the text, and the methods of [ApplicationModel] to be called. A view does not have to be a function: it is any callable object that receives a request and returns a response. [self.liste], a method associated with an object, is one such view: [Django] calls it with the request, and the method also receives its object ([self]), which is its section. To add a view to the doctor management and client management sections, simply write it here.

  • Lines 46–50: the fields affected by each business-logic data entry error: a duplicate username affects the “login” field; a name conflict affects the “first name” and “last name” fields. These fields will be highlighted in red;
  • Lines 55–64: The texts specific to each section, in a data class;
  • lines 68–78: the constructor. The last five parameters are functions ([Callable]): read the list, find, create, modify, or delete a person;
  • lines 81–89: the roads in the section. Decorators are called here as functions ([require_GET(self.liste)]: the decorated view [self.liste]): this is exactly what the syntax [@require_GET] does when placed above a function (Example 02). The prefix for the path and the route names is the section: the view [liste] becomes the routes [medecins_liste] ([/medecins]) and [clients_liste] ([/clients]);
  • lines 94–97: the list. The template is shared by both sections: it receives the text from the section and the URL from the add button;
  • lines 102–113: the add function. A single view for GET (the empty form, with the title [Mr] selected via [initial], Example 18) and POST (creation), as shown in Example 19. An invalid entry re-displays the form. A valid entry proceeds to the business layer, which may reject the write operation (due to a homonym or a login already in use); otherwise, a success message flashes and the user returns to the list (schema PRG). The message text is a lazy translation: [str(...)] translates it before the [%] operator inserts its parameters;
  • lines 120–139: the update, for a person who exists; otherwise, [Http404] returns a 404 page. [<int:id>] accepts only numbers for the [id] parameter (e.g., 02) and converts it to an integer. The GET form is pre-filled with the person’s values and their version; a POST form receives the input;
  • lines 145–152: deletion. The form requested confirmation in the browser (example 21). The person is retrieved before deletion for the success message (“Doctor Paul TATOU has been deleted.”);
  • lines 157–165: the form, for creation ([personne] equals [None]) or modification. A rejected form (invalid input or business rule violation) is returned with status code 422 (example 19). Here, [signaler] highlights the fields with errors in red;
  • lines 171–176: the business layer rejected the write operation. If a person has been deleted in the meantime (by another administrator): return to the list. Otherwise, the form is redisplayed directly (without redirection), as with an input error: it already contains the user’s input. Added to this are the business layer message (displayed at the bottom of the page, in the error area) and the fields to be highlighted in red;
  • lines 180–183: the parameters [%(nom)s] and [%(login)s] for success messages;
  • lines 193–215: the two objects. Each [lambda] calls the appropriate method of [ApplicationModel] when the request is made: the facade is not created when the module loads, but when it is first used.

docs.title: 11.17.7. web/views/inscription.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/inscription.py: “Create a Customer Account”: a patient who does not
# an account yet creates one themselves. Routes PUBLIQUES (we don’t have an account yet,
# by definition):
#
#    POST /registration/acc  ess "Create a Customer Account" button on the page
#                              authentication page: verifies the CAPTCHA from CETTE
#                              page, then opens the form
#    GE T /registrat        ion the form
#    POST /registrati        on creates the account, then returns to the login page
#
# The flow is protected against bots by the UN CAPTCHA on the
# authentication page:
#    1. The "Create a Customer Account" button sends the login form to
#       /registration/access; if the CAPTCHA is entered correctly, the server issues a
#       token (see security/passe_inscription.py);
#    2. Without a valid pass, /registration redirects to the
#       authentication page (decorator @passe_inscription_exige);
#    3. The token is consumed upon creation: a solved CAPTCHA allows
#       create a UN account;
#    4. Additionally, the number of accounts created per hour per IP address is limited
#       (see security/limiteur.py).
#
# The account created is exactly the one that ADMIN would create from the "Clients" page
# (same business-layer method: ajouter_client), except that the patient
# CHOISIT their username and password (required, with confirmation).
# =========================================================================

from urllib.parse import urlencode

from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_http_methods, require_POST

from metier.erreurs import MetierErreur
from securite import captchas, limiteur, passe_inscription
from securite.passe_inscription import passe_inscription_exige

from .. import outils
from ..application import application
from ..formulaires import InscriptionForm
from .personnes import CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER


# the message “too many accounts created,” in singular or plural form
def trop_de_comptes(minutes: int) -> str:
    return ngettext(
        "Trop de comptes ont été créés depuis votre connexion. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minute.",
        "Trop de comptes ont été créés depuis votre connexion. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minutes.",
        minutes) % {"minutes": minutes}


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /registration/login   fields: captcha_id, CAPTCHA (those on the
# authentication page; login and password, which are also sent, are ignored)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def acces(request):
    ip = outils.ip(request)
     # too many accounts created recently from this address: no need to proceed further
    minutes = limiteur.minutes_blocage_inscription(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        messages.error(request, trop_de_comptes(minutes))
        return redirect("login")
     # captcha missing or incorrect: return to the authentication page, with a
     # new image (one failure counts as a failed login attempt)
    if not captchas.verifier(request.POST.get("captcha_id", ""), request.POST.get("captcha", "")):
        limiteur.echec_login(ip, "")
        messages.error(request, _("Pour créer un compte, recopiez d'abord correctement les "
                                  "caractères de l'image, puis cliquez sur « Créer un compte client »."))
        return redirect("login")
     # Correct CAPTCHA: Grant access and display the form
    return passe_inscription.emettre(redirect("inscription"))


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /registration: the form; POST /registration: creation. The
# The token has been verified AVANT the view is called (@passe_inscription_exige).
# The form validates TOUTE the input (fields and password confirmation):
# The user corrects all errors at once
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
@passe_inscription_exige
def inscription(request):
    if request.method == "GET":
        return page(request, InscriptionForm(initial={"titre": "Mr"}))
    formulaire = InscriptionForm(request.POST)
    if not formulaire.is_valid():
        return page(request, formulaire)
    ip = outils.ip(request)
     # 1. Have too many accounts been created recently from this address?
    minutes = limiteur.minutes_blocage_inscription(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        return page(request, formulaire, trop_de_comptes(minutes))
     # 2. Account creation (customer + account USER, in a single transaction)
    donnees = formulaire.donnees()
    try:
        application().ajouter_client(donnees)
    except MetierErreur as e:
         # username or first name + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
        return page(request, formulaire, e.message, CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.code, []))
     # 3. The passcode has been used: it cannot be used to create a second account
    passe_inscription.consommer(request.COOKIES.get(passe_inscription.COOKIE))
    limiteur.inscription_reussie(ip)
     # 4. Return to the login page; username pre-filled
    messages.success(request, _("Votre compte a été créé. Vous pouvez vous connecter avec "
                                "le login %(login)s.") % {"login": donnees.login})
    url = f"{reverse('login')}?{urlencode({'login': donnees.login})}"
    return passe_inscription.effacer_cookie(redirect(url))


# The form; a rejected form: error code 422
def page(request, formulaire, erreur=None, champs_invalides=()):
    refuse = erreur is not None or (formulaire.is_bound and bool(formulaire.errors))
    return render(request, "inscription.html", {
        "titre_page": _("Créer un compte client"),
        "formulaire": formulaire.signaler(champs_invalides), "erreur": erreur,
    }, status=422 if refuse else 200)

The patient creates a customer account themselves. The flow is protected by a CAPTCHA, the same one used on the login page.

  • Lines 59–75: The “Create a Customer Account” button on the login page submits the login form to this address (which later becomes the template [login.html]). If too many accounts have been created recently from this address (IP), there is no need to proceed further. If the CAPTCHA is missing or incorrect: return to the login page with a new image and a message; the failure counts as a failed login attempt (with an empty username). If the CAPTCHA is correct: a token is stored in a cookie, and the user is redirected to the form;
  • lines 84–91: the form. The [@passe_inscription_exige] decorator (line 85) checks the token before calling the view. The order of the decorators matters: the one closest to the function is applied first; [require_http_methods], placed above, therefore rejects a prohibited method before any other checks. The form validates the entire input, including password confirmation: the user sees all their errors at once;
  • Lines 92–111: account creation. The client and their account are created using the same business-logic method as for the administrator ([ajouter_client]); only the username and password are chosen by the patient. If a username or a homonym is already taken: return to the form without consuming the token. Creating an account consumes the token (one solved CAPTCHA equals one account), counts toward the hourly limit, and redirects to the login page with the username pre-filled (parameter [?login=...], generated by [urlencode]), along with a success message. The pass cookie is cleared.

docs.title: 11.17.8. web/views/espace.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/espace.py: the patient’s pages (role USER), the one they
# sees immediately after logging in:
#
#    GE T /my-space               home page: [Gérer mon compte], [View a
#                                   calendar], and their upcoming appointment
#    POST /my-space/cancel        cancels the appointment SON
#    GE T /my-accou              nt account modification form
#    POST /my-accoun              t update
#    POST /my-account/delete      delete account (and its appointments)
#
# Golden rule for this module: the patient in question is TOUJOURS, the one associated with the token
# (outils.patient_connecte), never an identifier sent by the browser. A
# patient can therefore neither view, modify, nor cancel anything belonging to another
# patient, even by crafting their own requests.
#
# Any modification or deletion of the account requires the password ACTUEL:
# Someone who finds a session that has been left open cannot change the
# nor delete the account. Incorrect entries of the current password are
# counted as login failures (same limit).
#
# Security: All of these URL are reserved for the USER role (rule ^/my-
# security/acces.py).
# =========================================================================

from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_http_methods, require_POST

from metier.erreurs import MetierErreur
from modeles.models import Client
from securite import auth, limiteur

from .. import outils
from ..application import application
from ..formulaires import MonCompteForm
from ..modeles_vues import RendezVousVue
from .agenda import url_agenda
from .personnes import CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-space
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_GET
def espace(request):
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    rendez_vous = [RendezVousVue(
        rv.id,
        outils.formater_jour(rv.jour),
        rv.creneau.horaire(),
        rv.creneau.medecin.libelle(),
         # link to the doctor’s schedule for that day: the patient sees their name there
        url_agenda(rv.creneau.medecin_id, rv.jour))
        for rv in application().get_rv_a_venir_client(patient.id)]
    return render(request, "espace.html", {"titre_page": _("Mon espace"),
                                           "patient": patient.libelle(), "rendez_vous": rendez_vous})


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-space/cancel f  ield: idRv
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def annuler_rv(request):
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    id_rv = outils.entier_positif(request.POST.get("idRv"))
    rv = application().get_rv_by_id(id_rv) if id_rv is not None else None
     # a nonexistent appointment, and one for a AUTRE patient, receive the same
     # response: no information is disclosed about other patients’ appointments
    if rv is None or rv.client_id != patient.id:
        messages.error(request, _("Ce rendez-vous n'existe pas (ou plus)."))
    else:
        application().supprimer_rv(rv)
        messages.success(request, _("Rendez-vous annulé."))
    return redirect("espace")


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-account: the form, pre-filled with the patient’s information;
# POST /my-account: the update
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
def compte(request):
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    if request.method == "GET":
        return page(request, MonCompteForm(initial={
            "titre": patient.titre, "prenom": patient.prenom, "nom": patient.nom,
            "login": patient.compte.login, "version": patient.version}))
    formulaire = MonCompteForm(request.POST)
    if not formulaire.is_valid():
        return page(request, formulaire)
     # the current password; false: the message goes to SOUS the field (an error added
     # to the field by add_error), and at the bottom of the page
    erreur = verifier_mot_de_passe_actuel(request, patient, formulaire.cleaned_data["current_password"])
    if erreur is not None:
        formulaire.add_error("current_password", erreur)
        return page(request, formulaire, erreur)
    try:
        client = application().modifier_client(patient.id, formulaire.donnees())
    except MetierErreur as e:
        return page(request, formulaire, e.message, CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.code, []))
     # the login and display name are DANS the token: a new one is issued; otherwise
     # the navigation bar would retain the old name
    messages.success(request, _("Votre compte a été modifié."))
    return auth.poser_jeton(redirect("espace"), client.compte)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-account/delete f  ield: current_password
# The account, the client, and TOUS their appointments all disappear together, then the
# The patient is disconnected.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def supprimer_compte(request):
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    erreur = verifier_mot_de_passe_actuel(request, patient, request.POST.get("current_password", ""))
    if erreur is not None:
        messages.error(request, erreur)
        return redirect("compte")
    application().supprimer_client(patient.id)
    messages.success(request, _("Votre compte a été supprimé."))
    return auth.effacer_jeton(redirect("login"))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions
# the account page; a form was rejected: code 422
def page(request, formulaire, erreur=None, champs_invalides=()):
    refuse = erreur is not None or (formulaire.is_bound and bool(formulaire.errors))
    return render(request, "compte.html", {
        "titre_page": _("Gérer mon compte"),
        "formulaire": formulaire.signaler(champs_invalides), "erreur": erreur,
    }, status=422 if refuse else 200)


# None if the current password is correct; otherwise, the error message
def verifier_mot_de_passe_actuel(request, patient: Client, mot_de_passe: str) -> str | None:
    ip = outils.ip(request)
    login = patient.compte.login
    minutes = limiteur.minutes_blocage_login(ip, login)
    if minutes > 0:
        return ngettext("Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minute.",
                        "Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minutes.",
                        minutes) % {"minutes": minutes}
    if not mot_de_passe or auth.valider(login, mot_de_passe) is None:
        limiteur.echec_login(ip, login)
        return _("Mot de passe actuel incorrect.")
    return None

The patient’s personal pages. The golden rule of this module: the patient in question is always the one associated with the token ([outils.patient_connecte]), never an identifier sent by the browser. A patient cannot therefore view, modify, or cancel information belonging to another patient, even if they generate their own requests.

  • Lines 46–58: My Space: the patient’s name and their upcoming appointments, formatted ([RendezVousVue]), each with a link to the doctor’s schedule for that day. The function [url_agenda] is part of the calendar module (line 39, [from .agenda import url_agenda]);
  • lines 64–76: the cancellation of his appointment. Both a nonexistent appointment and another patient’s appointment receive the same response: no information is disclosed about other patients’ appointments (not even their existence);
  • lines 83–92: the “Manage My Account” form, pre-filled with the patient’s information, and its submission;
  • lines 95–106: the modification. Any modification requires the current password: someone who found a session left open would be unable to change the password or do anything else. If the current password is incorrect, the form is redisplayed, with the message below the field and at the bottom of the page. [add_error(champ, message)] adds an error to a field, as if validation had detected it (example 19). After the modification, a new token is generated: the login and the displayed name are included in the token, and the navigation bar would otherwise retain the old name until the next login;
  • lines 114–123: deletion of the account, the client, and all their appointments, using the same business-logic method as for the administrator. This second form on the page is hand-coded (a single field: the current password). The patient is then logged out (the token cookie is cleared);
  • lines 137–148: Verification of the current password. This is subject to the attempt limiter, just like a login: without this, someone with an open session could try thousands of passwords via the “Manage My Account” form and discover the correct one.

docs.title: 11.18. The Templates
docs.text: The templates in the [templates] folder (configuration [TEMPLATES] derived from [config/settings.py]): a parent template, fragments, named form fragments, and pages.

docs.title: 11.18.1.1. templates/layout.html
docs.text:
<!doctype html>
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/layout.html
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Le gabarit PARENT de toutes les pages (cf. exemple 15) : chaque page
  (agenda.html, login.html...) l'ÉTEND ({% extends %}) et remplit son bloc
  [contenu].

  Django ÉCHAPPE tout ce qu'il affiche avec {{ ... }} (les caractères < > & " '
  deviennent < >...) : protection contre l'injection de HTML via un nom
  saisi, par exemple. Pour insérer du HTML tel quel, il faut le demander
  explicitement (filtre safe, cf. fragments/captcha.html).

  Messages : un succès s'affiche en HAUT de la page, une erreur en BAS, sur fond
  rose léger (balises zone_succes et zone_erreurs, cf. web/templatetags/rdv.py).

  Le gabarit partage les variables de la page : [titre_page] (le titre de la
  page, transmis par la vue, déjà traduit). LANGUAGE_CODE : la langue de la
  requête (cf. web/middleware.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load static i18n rdv %}
<html lang="{{ LANGUAGE_CODE }}">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>{{ titre_page }} - RdvMedecins</title>
  {# static: the URL from a file in the static folder #}
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css' %}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/styles.css' %}">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-4">
    {% include "fragments/navbar.html" %}
    {% zone_succes %}
    <main>
      {% block contenu %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
    {% zone_erreurs %}
  </div>
  {# the "Are you sure?" window, hidden until needed #}
  {% include "fragments/confirmation.html" %}
  <script src="{% static 'js/app.js' %}"></script>
</body>
</html>

The parent template for all pages (Example 15): each page extends it ([{% extends "layout.html" %}]) and fills in its [contenu] block (line 38).

  • Line 23: the tag libraries used: [static] (static files), [i18n] (translations, Example 22), and [rdv], ours (web layer, above). A parent template does not pass its libraries on to the templates that extend it: each page loads the ones it needs;
  • line 24: the page’s language, [fr] or [en]: the active language of the request, set by the [FixerLangue] middleware;
  • line 28: the page title, already translated by the view, which passes it in the variable [titre_page];
  • lines 30–31: the [{% static %}] tag renders the URL from a file in the [static] folder (Example 15);
  • lines 35–40: the navigation bar, the success messages at the top of the page, the page content, and the error area at the bottom of the page. The navigation bar snippet is inserted by [{% include %}] (Example 15): it accesses the page’s variables. The two message areas are the inclusion tags from [web/templatetags/rdv.py];
  • lines 43–44: the “Are you sure?” window, hidden until needed, and the script that displays it.

The header comment (lines 2–22) is a [{% comment %}] tag: a template comment that can span multiple lines ([{# ... #}] fits on a single line, example 14). It is written after [<!doctype html>]: the first line of the sent page must be the document type declaration. The DTL escapes everything it displays using [{{ ... }}] (Example 14): a user-entered name containing HTML ([<script>]) is displayed as-is, without being interpreted. This prevents HTML (XSS) from being injected effortlessly into all pages.

docs.title: 11.18.1.2. templates/fragments/navbar.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/navbar.html - la barre de navigation.

  Titre, FR/EN, rôle, nom, déconnexion - et le menu, dont les entrées dépendent
  du rôle : elles sont calculées par le processeur de contexte web/contextes.py
  (variable menu), avec, pour chacune, son URL, son libellé, et si elle est celle
  de la page courante (classe "active").

  utilisateur : l'utilisateur connecté, ou None (cf. web/contextes.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">RdvMedecins</span>

  <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
    {% for entree in menu %}
    <li class="nav-item">
      <a class="nav-link{% if entree.active %} active{% endif %}" href="{{ entree.url }}">{{ entree.libelle }}</a>
    </li>
    {% endfor %}
  </ul>

  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
    {# FR / EN: simple links (GET /language/fr), with the active language highlighted #}
    {% get_available_languages as langues %}
    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label="FR / EN">
      {% for code, nom in langues %}
      <a class="btn {% if code == LANGUAGE_CODE %}btn-light{% else %}btn-outline-light{% endif %}"
         href="{% url 'langue' code %}">{{ code|upper }}</a>
      {% endfor %}
    </div>

    {% if utilisateur %}
    <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{{ utilisateur.role }}</span>
    <span class="text-white">{{ utilisateur.nom }}</span>
    {# Logout is a POST: a form reduced to its button (and the anti-CSRF token) #}
    <form method="post" action="{% url 'logout' %}" class="m-0">
      {% csrf_token %}
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light">{% translate "Se déconnecter" %}</button>
    </form>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</nav>

The navigation bar. It simply displays what the [web/contextes.py] context processor has prepared: the logged-in user ([utilisateur]), and the menu items ([menu]), which depend on the role.

  • lines 17–23: the menu, with each entry having its own URL and label; the [active] class of [Bootstrap] highlights the entry for the currently displayed page;
  • Lines 27–32: the FR / EN buttons, simple links ([/langue/fr]), with the active language highlighted. [{% get_available_languages as langues %}] (library [i18n]) stores the setting [LANGUAGES]—a list of (code, name) pairs—in the variable [langues], which the loop unpacks ([{% for code, nom in langues %}]); the filter [upper] capitalizes the code. [{% url 'langue' code %}] creates URL for a route that has a parameter (example 15);
  • Lines 35–43: For a logged-in user, their role, name, and the logout button. Logout is a request for POST: a form reduced to just its button, with its anti-CSRF token ([{% csrf_token %}], Example 21).

docs.title: 11.18.1.3. templates/fragments/succes.html and erreurs.html
docs.text:
{# templates/fragments/succes.html - messages from SUCCÈS (tag zone_succes, see web/templatetags/rdv.py) #}
{% for texte in textes %}
<div class="alert alert-success" role="status">{{ texte }}</div>
{% endfor %}

{% comment %}
  templates/fragments/erreurs.html - la zone d'erreur, en BAS de chaque page, sur
  fond rose léger (classe .zone-erreur, cf. static/css/styles.css). Les messages
  sont rassemblés par la balise zone_erreurs (cf. web/templatetags/rdv.py).
  role="alert" : un lecteur d'écran annonce le message dès l'affichage de la page,
  même s'il se trouve en bas.
{% endcomment %}
{% if textes %}
<div class="zone-erreur" role="alert">
  {% for texte in textes %}
  <div>{{ texte }}</div>
  {% endfor %}
</div>
{% endif %}

The two inclusion tag templates [zone_succes] and [zone_erreurs] (web layer, above): they receive the list [textes], prepared by the tag, and display it. [role="status"]: A screen reader announces the success message. [role="alert"]: It announces the error section as soon as the page is displayed, even if it is at the bottom. The error section remains anchored at the bottom of the window when the page is long (see the stylesheet below).

docs.title: 11.18.1.4. templates/fragments/confirmation.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/confirmation.html - la fenêtre modale "Êtes-vous sûr ?"
  (cf. exemple 21).

  Elle remplace la boîte window.confirm() du navigateur, qu'on ne peut ni mettre
  en forme, ni traduire (ses boutons restent dans la langue du navigateur, pas
  dans celle de la page).

  Une SEULE fenêtre pour toute la page, cachée (d-none) au départ. Ses libellés
  sont traduits ici, par le serveur, comme le reste de la page ; le petit script
  static/js/app.js se contente de l'afficher, d'y placer le message propre au
  formulaire (attribut data-confirmation), et d'envoyer le formulaire si
  l'utilisateur confirme.
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div id="modale-confirmation" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
       aria-labelledby="modale-confirmation-titre" aria-describedby="modale-confirmation-message">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title" id="modale-confirmation-titre">{% translate "Confirmation" %}</h5>
          <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-action="non" aria-label="{% translate 'Fermer' %}"></button>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="modale-confirmation-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          {# "No, go back" instead of "Cancel": the question is sometimes "Cancel this appointment?" #}
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="non">{% translate "Non, revenir" %}</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="oui">{% translate "Oui, confirmer" %}</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

The “Are you sure?” modal window from Example 21, which replaces the browser’s [window.confirm()] dialog box: this dialog box does not format correctly, and its buttons remain in the browser’s language, not the page’s language. A single window for the entire page, initially hidden (class [d-none] derived from [Bootstrap]); its labels are translated by the server, just like the rest of the page. The [static/js/app.js] script displays it, places the message from the form to be confirmed inside it (its [data-confirmation] attribute), and submits the form if the user confirms. The "Cancel" button is labeled “No, go back” rather than “Cancel”: the question is sometimes “Cancel this appointment?”, and a “Cancel” button would be ambiguous in that context. The attributes [role="alertdialog"], [aria-modal], [aria-labelledby], and [aria-describedby] describe the window to screen readers: a dialog box awaiting a response, its title, and its message.

docs.title: 11.18.1.5. templates/fragments/reservation.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/reservation.html - la fenêtre de réservation de l'agenda.
