  Les VRAIES classes Bootstrap d'une fenêtre modale (.modal, .modal-backdrop...),
  rendues visibles "en dur" (show d-block) plutôt que par le JavaScript de
  Bootstrap. C'est le SERVEUR qui décide de l'afficher (paramètre &reserver=... de
  l'URL), et la fermer revient à suivre un lien vers la même page sans ce
  paramètre.

  Le fragment lit directement les variables de la page qui l'insère
  (reservation, id_medecin, jour, url_retour).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
<div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="titre-reservation">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <form method="post" action="{% url 'agenda_reserver' %}" class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title" id="titre-reservation">{% translate "Réserver ce créneau" %}</h5>
        <a class="btn-close" href="{{ url_retour }}" aria-label="{% translate 'Fermer' %}"></a>
      </div>

      <div class="modal-body">
        <p>{% blocktranslate with horaire=reservation.horaire %}Créneau de {{ horaire }}{% endblocktranslate %}</p>

        {# what the server needs to know in addition to the selected patient #}
        {% csrf_token %}
        <input type="hidden" name="idMedecin" value="{{ id_medecin }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="jour" value="{{ jour }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="idCreneau" value="{{ reservation.id_creneau }}">

        {# A patient is booking for themselves: no list to choose from (and the server ignores any idClient anyway) #}
        {% if reservation.patient %}
        <p class="mb-0">
          <span>{% translate "Patient" %}</span> :
          <strong>{{ reservation.patient }}</strong>
        </p>
        {% else %}
        <label class="form-label" for="idClient">{% translate "Patient" %}</label>
        <select id="idClient" name="idClient" class="form-select" required autofocus>
          <option value="">{% translate "-- choisir un patient --" %}</option>
          {% for client in reservation.clients %}
          <option value="{{ client.id }}">{{ client.libelle }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
        {% endif %}
      </div>

      <div class="modal-footer">
        <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ url_retour }}">{% translate "Annuler" %}</a>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Confirmer" %}</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>

The calendar booking window. It uses the actual classes of a modal window from [Bootstrap] ([modal], [modal-backdrop]...), but made visible "hard-coded" ([show d-block]), rather than via the [JavaScript] from [Bootstrap]: it is the server that decides to display it when URL contains [&reserver=...]. Closing it (using the X or the Cancel button) is equivalent to following a link to the same page without that parameter ([url_retour]).

  • Line 26: [{% blocktranslate with horaire=reservation.horaire %}]: a translated text that contains a variable (example 22). In a [blocktranslate], only simple variables are allowed ([{{ horaire }}], not [{{ reservation.horaire }}]): the [with] clause creates one;
  • lines 29–32: the anti-CSRF token, and what the server needs to know: the doctor, the day, and the time slot;
  • lines 35–48: a patient makes a reservation for themselves: their name, with no list to choose from (and the server ignores any [idClient] field anyway). The administrator and doctors select the patient from a list; [required] and [autofocus]: the browser requires a selection and places the cursor in the list.

docs.title: 11.18.1.6. templates/fragments/captcha.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/captcha.html - le captcha de la page d'authentification
  (cf. securite/captchas.py). Il protège à la fois la connexion et l'accès à la
  création de compte (bouton "Créer un compte client"). Il lit la variable
  [captcha] de la page.

  captcha.svg|safe : l'image SVG est insérée TELLE QUELLE dans la page, sans
  échappement. C'est sans danger ici parce que ce SVG est fabriqué par le serveur
  lui-même et ne contient rien qui vienne de l'utilisateur - on ne ferait JAMAIS
  cela avec une saisie.

  Le champ caché captcha_id dit au serveur QUEL captcha vérifier ; la bonne
  réponse, elle, n'est jamais envoyée au navigateur. "Autre image" recharge
  simplement la page ({% url 'login' %} : l'URL de la page, sans ses paramètres).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="captcha">{% translate "Recopiez les caractères de l'image" %}</label>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
    <div class="captcha-image" role="img" aria-label="{% translate 'Image de vérification anti-robots' %}">{{ captcha.svg|safe }}</div>
    <a class="small" href="{% url 'login' %}">{% translate "Autre image" %}</a>
  </div>
  <input type="hidden" name="captcha_id" value="{{ captcha.id }}">
  <input id="captcha" name="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off"
         spellcheck="false" required class="form-control">
  <div class="form-text">{% translate "Majuscules ou minuscules, peu importe." %}</div>
</div>

The CAPTCHA (example 27). [captcha.svg|safe] inserts the image SVG as-is, without escaping it: otherwise, the browser would display its code XML. This is safe here because this SVG is generated by the server and contains nothing provided by the user: we would never do this with user input. The hidden field [captcha_id] tells the server which CAPTCHA to verify; the response itself is never sent to the browser. The “Other image” link reloads the login page—and thus the CAPTCHA. The attributes of the input fields ([autocomplete="off"], [autocapitalize="off"], [spellcheck="false"]) prevent the browser from suggesting a previous entry and the phone’s keyboard from capitalizing letters or correcting spelling.

docs.title: 11.18.2.1. templates/forms/champ.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  templates/formulaires/champ.html - un champ complet d'un formulaire : libellé,
  zone de saisie, puis son message d'erreur ou son aide (cf. exemple 18 et le
  réglage FORM_RENDERER). La zone de saisie est encadrée en rouge (classe
  is-invalid) par la méthode signaler du formulaire (cf. web/formulaires.py).
{% endcomment %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="{{ field.id_for_label }}">{{ field.label }}</label>
  {{ field }}
  {% if field.errors %}<div class="invalid-feedback d-block" id="{{ field.auto_id }}_error">{% for erreur in field.errors %}{{ erreur }}{% if not forloop.last %}<br>{% endif %}{% endfor %}</div>{% endif %}
  {% if field.help_text and not field.errors %}<div class="form-text" id="{{ field.auto_id }}_helptext">{{ field.help_text }}</div>{% endif %}
</div>

The template for a complete field—that of the [RenduBootstrap] rendering engine (web layer, above)—as shown in Example 18: the label, the input field ([{{ field }}], with the classes CSS provided by the form), followed by the error message or, if none, the help text. The classes [invalid-feedback] (the message in red) and [form-text] (the help text in gray) are those of [Bootstrap]; [d-block] displays the message even if the input field is not immediately preceding it. A field may have multiple errors: they are separated by a line break ([forloop.last], example 14).

The identifiers [..._error] and [..._helptext] are not chosen at random: these are the ones that [Django] refers to in the [aria-describedby] attributes of the input field, with [aria-invalid] for a field with an error. A screen reader thus reads the error message or help text along with the field:

<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="id_prenom">Prénom</label>
  <input type="text" name="prenom" maxlength="20" class="form-control is-invalid" required aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="id_prenom_error" id="id_prenom">
  <div class="invalid-feedback d-block" id="id_prenom_error">Le prénom est obligatoire.</div>
</div>

The red border ([is-invalid]) was added by the form’s [signaler] method; [maxlength] and [required] by [Django], based on the field’s options. The [required] attribute does not prevent an empty form from being submitted: the application’s forms carry the [novalidate] attribute (see below); validation is performed by the server.

docs.title: 11.18.2.2. templates/macros.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  templates/macros.html - les fragments nommés des formulaires (cf. exemple 15).

  identite : les champs d'identité (titre, prénom, nom), communs à trois
  formulaires : médecin/client de l'ADMIN, "Créer un compte client" et "Gérer mon
  compte". Il lit la variable [formulaire] de la page qui l'insère :
  {% include "macros.html#identite" %}.
{% endcomment %}
{% partialdef identite %}
  {{ formulaire.titre.as_field_group }}
  <div class="row g-3">
    <div class="col-sm-6">{{ formulaire.prenom.as_field_group }}</div>
    <div class="col-sm-6">{{ formulaire.nom.as_field_group }}</div>
  </div>
{% endpartialdef %}

A named fragment ([{% partialdef %}], example 15), used by the three pages that display a “person” form: the identification fields, the title, then the first name and last name side by side (the grid from [Bootstrap]: [row], [col-sm-6]). Each field is rendered by [as_field_group] (Example 18), that is, by the template [champ.html]. A page inserts it using [{% include "macros.html#identite" %}]: the fragment reads the variable [formulaire] from the page.

docs.title: 11.18.3.1. templates/login.html
docs.text:
{% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/login.html - le formulaire de connexion (cf. web/vues/auth.py).
  Un <form> HTML ordinaire, écrit à la main : le navigateur envoie lui-même login,
  mot de passe et réponse au captcha en POST /login, sans JavaScript. En cas
  d'échec, le serveur renvoie CETTE page, avec le login déjà saisi, un NOUVEAU
  captcha et l'erreur, affichée en bas de page par le gabarit parent.
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-sm-8 col-md-6 col-lg-5">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{% translate "Connexion" %}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="{% url 'login' %}">
        {% csrf_token %}
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{% translate "Login" %}</label>
          {# autofocus: a Boolean attribute, set if the condition is true. The cursor goes to the first field to be filled in #}
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
                 value="{{ login }}" required{% if not login %} autofocus{% endif %}>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{% translate "Mot de passe" %}</label>
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" class="form-control"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required{% if login %} autofocus{% endif %}>
        </div>

        {% include "fragments/captcha.html" %}

        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{% translate "Se connecter" %}</button>

        {% comment %}
          pas encore de compte : un patient peut en créer un lui-même. Ce n'est PAS
          un simple lien : c'est un second bouton d'envoi de CE formulaire, qui part
          vers une autre adresse (formaction). Le serveur y vérifie le captcha
          ci-dessus avant d'ouvrir la page de création de compte (cf.
          web/vues/inscription.py). formnovalidate : le navigateur n'exige pas
          login et mot de passe (inutiles pour créer un compte). Entrée dans un
          champ déclenche toujours le PREMIER bouton du formulaire, "Se connecter".
        {% endcomment %}
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-primary w-100 mt-3"
                formaction="{% url 'inscription_acces' %}" formnovalidate>{% translate "Créer un compte client" %}</button>
        <div class="form-text text-center">{% translate "Pour créer un compte, recopiez d'abord les caractères de l'image." %}</div>
      </form>

      <div class="text-muted small mt-3">
        <span>{% translate "Comptes de démonstration (mot de passe = login) :" %}</span>
        <ul class="mb-0 mt-1">
          <li><code>admin</code> - <span>{% translate "rôle ADMIN : rendez-vous + gestion des médecins et des clients" %}</span></li>
          <li><code>pelissier</code>, <code>tatou</code>, <code>dupont</code> - <span>{% translate "rôle DOCTOR : prise et annulation de rendez-vous" %}</span></li>
          <li><code>martin</code>, <code>durand</code>, <code>bistrou</code>, <code>german</code> - <span>{% translate "rôle USER (patients) : réservation pour eux-mêmes, gestion de leur compte" %}</span></li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

The login form, a hand-coded [<form>], is sent via POST to [/login]. The [{% extends %}] tag is the first in the template (line 1), as required by DTL; the comment follows.

  • Lines 24–30: The entered login is redisplayed after a failed attempt ([login]). The attribute [autofocus] places the cursor in the first field to be filled in: the username if it is empty, the password otherwise (after a failed login attempt or after creating an account). A Boolean attribute is either present or absent: [{% if not login %} autofocus{% endif %}];
  • line 33: the CAPTCHA;
  • lines 46–47: the “Create a Customer Account” button is not a link; it is a second button that submits the same form to a different address (button attribute [formaction]). The server verifies the CAPTCHA there before opening the account creation page ([inscription.acces]). [formnovalidate]: The browser does not require a username and password (attributes [required]), as they are not needed to create an account. Pressing the Enter key in a field always triggers the first form submission button: Log In;
  • lines 51–58: demo accounts, for testing.

docs.title: 11.18.3.2. templates/agenda.html
docs.text:
{% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/agenda.html - la page principale (cf. web/vues/agenda.py).
  Trois blocs :
    1. le choix du médecin et du jour ;
    2. l'agenda ;
    3. la fenêtre de réservation (fragment reservation).
  Une éventuelle erreur (date invalide, médecin inconnu) est affichée en bas de
  la page par le gabarit parent (balise zone_erreurs).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
  {# 1. Selecting a doctor and date: a GET form, which simply reloads this page with ?idMedecin=...&day=... #}
  <form method="get" action="{% url 'agenda' %}" class="card p-3 mb-3">
    <div class="row g-2 align-items-end">
      <div class="col-sm-5">
        <label class="form-label" for="idMedecin">{% translate "Médecin" %}</label>
        <select id="idMedecin" name="idMedecin" class="form-select" required>
          <option value="">{% translate "-- choisir un médecin --" %}</option>
          {% for medecin in medecins %}
          <option value="{{ medecin.id }}"{% if medecin.selectionne %} selected{% endif %}>{{ medecin.libelle }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-4">
        <label class="form-label" for="jour">{% translate "Jour" %}</label>
        <input id="jour" name="jour" type="date" class="form-control" value="{{ jour }}" required>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-3">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{% translate "Voir l'agenda" %}</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </form>

  {# Patient who already has an upcoming appointment: why there is no “Book” button #}
  {% if info %}
  <div class="alert alert-info">
    <span>{{ info }}</span>
    <a href="{% url 'espace' %}" class="alert-link">{% translate "Mon espace" %}</a>
  </div>
  {% endif %}

  {# 2. The calendar #}
  {% if agenda %}
  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{% translate "Agenda du" %} {{ agenda.jour }} - {{ agenda.medecin }}</h5>

    {% if agenda.lignes %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{% translate "Créneau" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Statut" %}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {% for ligne in agenda.lignes %}
        <tr{% if ligne.reservable %} class="creneau-libre"{% endif %}>
          <td>{{ ligne.horaire }}</td>
          <td>
            {% comment %}
              [patient] n'est renseigné que si l'utilisateur a le droit de voir ce
              nom (ADMIN, DOCTOR, ou le patient pour SON rendez-vous) - sinon,
              simplement « Réservé »
            {% endcomment %}
            {% if ligne.libre %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-success">{% translate "Libre" %}</span>
            {% elif ligne.patient %}
            <span class="badge {% if ligne.moi %}text-bg-primary{% else %}text-bg-secondary{% endif %}">{{ ligne.patient }}</span>
            {% else %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">{% translate "Réservé" %}</span>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
          <td>
            {% comment %}
              les boutons affichés ont été décidés par la vue (reservable, id_rv)
              selon le rôle de l'utilisateur. "Réserver" est un simple lien : il
              rouvre cette page avec la fenêtre de réservation de ce créneau
            {% endcomment %}
            {% if ligne.reservable %}
            <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" href="{{ ligne.url_reserver }}">{% translate "Réserver" %}</a>
            {% endif %}
            {# "Cancel" MODIFIE data: so it’s a POST #}
            {% if ligne.id_rv %}
            <form method="post" action="{% url 'agenda_annuler' %}" class="m-0"
                  data-confirmation="{% translate 'Annuler ce rendez-vous ?' %}">
              {% csrf_token %}
              <input type="hidden" name="idRv" value="{{ ligne.id_rv }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="idMedecin" value="{{ id_medecin }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="jour" value="{{ jour }}">
              <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{% translate "Annuler" %}</button>
            </form>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{% translate "Ce médecin n'a aucun créneau horaire." %}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
  {% else %}
  <p class="text-muted">{% translate "Choisissez un médecin et un jour, puis cliquez sur « Voir l'agenda »." %}</p>
  {% endif %}

  {# 3. The booking window, only if the URL contains &reserver=... #}
  {% if reservation %}
  {% include "fragments/reservation.html" %}
  {% endif %}
{% endblock %}

The main page. Three sections: selecting a doctor and a day, the calendar, and the booking window.

  • Lines 17–36: Selecting a doctor and a day: a GET form (example 17), which reloads the page with [?idMedecin=...&jour=...] in the URL. The day is a [type="date"] field: the browser displays a calendar and sends the date in [aaaa-mm-jj] format, regardless of how it displays it ([30/09/2026] in French); the initial value ([value]) is written in this same format;
  • lines 39–44: for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment, why isn’t there a “Book” button with a link to “My Account”?
  • Lines 70–76: The slot status: Available (in green), the patient’s name (in blue for an appointment booked by the logged-in patient, in gray otherwise), or “Reserved.” The template does not determine anything: [ligne.patient] is only displayed if the user has permission to view that name;
  • lines 84–86: “Reserve” is a simple link: it reopens the page with the reservation window for that time slot ([ligne.url_reserver]). It does not modify anything: a GET is sufficient;
  • lines 88–97: “Cancel” modifies data: it is a POST form (example 21), with its anti-CSRF token, the appointment to be canceled, and information to return to the same page (the doctor, the day). The [data-confirmation] attribute causes the page’s script to request confirmation; its text is represented by [{% translate %}], enclosed in single quotes within the attribute, which is itself enclosed in double quotes;
  • lines 112–114: the booking window, if URL requests it (and if the time slot is bookable).

{% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/personnes/liste.html - la liste des médecins OU des clients (ADMIN).
  Un seul gabarit pour les deux : les textes propres à chacun arrivent dans
  [textes], et [section] ("medecins" ou "clients") donne le début des noms des
  routes (cf. web/vues/personnes.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
  <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
    <h4 class="mb-0">{{ textes.titre }}</h4>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="{{ url_ajout }}">{{ textes.ajouter }}</a>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    {% if personnes %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle mb-0">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{% translate "Titre" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Prénom" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Nom" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Login" %}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {# personne.compte.login: the account, loaded by the same request (select_related) #}
        {% for personne in personnes %}
        <tr>
          <td>{{ personne.titre }}</td>
          <td>{{ personne.prenom }}</td>
          <td>{{ personne.nom }}</td>
          <td><code>{{ personne.compte.login }}</code></td>
          <td class="text-end">
            <div class="d-inline-flex gap-2">
              {# section|add:"_modification": "medecins_modification", the route name #}
              <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary"
                 href="{% url section|add:'_modification' personne.id %}">{% translate "Modifier" %}</a>
              {# data-confirmation: a confirmation window will open before the form is submitted (see static/js/app.js) #}
              <form method="post" action="{% url section|add:'_supprimer' personne.id %}" class="m-0"
                    data-confirmation="{{ textes.confirmer_suppression }}">
                {% csrf_token %}
                <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{% translate "Supprimer" %}</button>
              </form>
            </div>
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ textes.vide }}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

The list of doctors or clients: the text specific to each one is stored in the variable [textes], and the route names are generated from the section name: [section|add:'_modification'] yields [medecins_modification] or [clients_modification] (the filter [add] adds two numbers or, as in this case, concatenates two strings). [{% url %}] thus accepts, as a route name, a calculated expression followed by the route parameters ([personne.id]). [personne.compte.login]: the account login, loaded along with the list (layer DAO), and stored with it in the cache. The Delete button is a POST form, with confirmation.

docs.title: 11.18.3.4. templates/people/formulaire.html
docs.text:
{% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/personnes/formulaire.html - création OU modification d'un médecin ou
  d'un client (ADMIN), avec le formulaire PersonneForm.

  Quand la saisie est refusée (champ vide, login déjà pris...), la vue réaffiche
  CETTE page, et le gabarit montre :
    - les valeurs déjà saisies (sauf le mot de passe) ;
    - les champs fautifs encadrés en rouge (classe Bootstrap "is-invalid") ;
    - sous un champ refusé par la validation, son message ;
    - le message d'erreur de la page, EN BAS de la page (balise zone_erreurs).
  Le formulaire est envoyé à l'URL de la page elle-même (pas d'attribut action).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ titre_page }}</h5>

      <form method="post" novalidate>
        {% csrf_token %}
        {# title, first name, last name: a section common to three forms #}
        {% include "macros.html#identite" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{% translate "Compte utilisateur" %}</h6>
        {{ formulaire.login.as_field_group }}
        {# never pre-filled: the password is never sent back to the browser #}
        {{ formulaire.password.as_field_group }}
        {# on edit only: the record version, in a hidden field (the optimistic lock) #}
        {% if formulaire.version %}{{ formulaire.version }}{% endif %}

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Enregistrer" %}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ url_liste }}">{% translate "Retour à la liste" %}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

Creating or modifying a doctor or a client using the [PersonneForm] form.

  • Line 24: a POST form without the [action] attribute: it is sent to the URL of the page itself ([/medecins/ajouter] or [/medecins/3/modifier]). [novalidate] disables browser validation ([required], [maxlength]...) when the form is submitted: the server performs the validation, and its result is authoritative (example 19);
  • line 27: title, first name, and last name, via the fragment [identite];
  • lines 30–32: the username and password, which are never pre-filled. Their tooltips differ between creation and modification (depending on the form builder);
  • line 34: for editing only, the hidden version field (the optimistic lock). [{{ formulaire.version }}] populates the input field alone, without a label: [<input type="hidden" name="version" value="1" id="id_version">]. When creating a record, the form does not have a [version] field: the variable is empty, and the test evaluates to false.

Errors in the form itself that do not involve any fields ([non_field_errors], example 19) do not need to be displayed: the form does not generate any, and an invalid anti-CSRF token is rejected before the view (the 419 page).

“My Account,” the patient’s home page: two large cards (“Manage My Account,” “View Schedule”), and their upcoming appointment.

  • line 13: [{% blocktranslate %}Bonjour {{ patient }}{% endblocktranslate %}]: a translated text containing a variable ([Hello %(patient)s] in the English dictionary);
  • lines 37–55: [{% for %}] ... [{% empty %}] (Example 14) is a loop, followed by what to display if the list is empty. Normally, a patient has at most one upcoming appointment; however, the page is capable of displaying multiple appointments. [forloop.last] (Example 14): the last item has no separator;
  • lines 46–51: each appointment has a cancellation form (POST, with confirmation), which sends only its ID: the server will verify that it belongs to the logged-in patient.

docs.title: 11.18.3.7. templates/compte.html
docs.text:
{% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/compte.html - "Gérer mon compte" (rôle USER). Deux formulaires
  indépendants sur la même page :
    1. la modification (identité, login, nouveau mot de passe facultatif), avec
       le formulaire MonCompteForm ;
    2. la suppression du compte - qui annule aussi ses rendez-vous : un
       formulaire écrit à la main.
  L'un comme l'autre exigent le mot de passe ACTUEL (champ current_password).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">

    {# 1. edit; no validation: validation is performed by SERVEUR (see example 19) #}
    <div class="card p-4 mb-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{% translate "Gérer mon compte" %}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="{% url 'compte' %}" novalidate>
        {% csrf_token %}
        {% include "macros.html#identite" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{% translate "Compte utilisateur" %}</h6>
        {{ formulaire.login.as_field_group }}
        <div class="row g-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ formulaire.password.as_field_group }}</div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ formulaire.confirmation.as_field_group }}</div>
        </div>
        {{ formulaire.current_password.as_field_group }}
        {# the record version: a hidden field (the optimistic lock) #}
        {{ formulaire.version }}

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Enregistrer" %}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{% url 'espace' %}">{% translate "Retour à mon espace" %}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>

    {% comment %}
      2. suppression. Le champ du mot de passe a le même NOM que celui du premier
      formulaire (current_password), mais un autre id : deux éléments d'une même
      page ne peuvent pas avoir le même id
    {% endcomment %}
    <div class="card p-4 border-danger">
      <h5 class="card-title text-danger mb-1">{% translate "Supprimer mon compte" %}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small">{% translate "Votre compte sera définitivement supprimé, ainsi que tous vos rendez-vous." %}</p>
      <form method="post" action="{% url 'compte_supprimer' %}" class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-2 align-items-end"
            data-confirmation="{% translate 'Supprimer définitivement votre compte ? Votre rendez-vous éventuel sera annulé.' %}">
        {% csrf_token %}
        <div class="flex-grow-1">
          <label class="form-label" for="mot_de_passe_suppression">{% translate "Mot de passe actuel" %}</label>
          <input id="mot_de_passe_suppression" name="current_password" type="password" maxlength="72"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required class="form-control">
        </div>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-danger">{% translate "Supprimer mon compte" %}</button>
      </form>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

“Manage My Account”: two independent forms on the same page.

  • Lines 20–42: the update, using the [MonCompteForm] form: the identity fields, the login, the new password and its confirmation (optional), the current password (required), and the hidden version field;
  • Lines 49–62: Account deletion, a handwritten form with its own field for the current password and a confirmation field. The field has the same name as the one on the first form ([current_password]), but a different ID: two elements on a page cannot have the same ID, as indicated by the attribute [for] for a label. The two forms are independent: the browser sends only the fields from the form whose button was clicked.

docs.title: 11.19. Static files
docs.text: The [static] folder contains the files that the server sends as-is (example 15): [Bootstrap] ([lib/bootstrap], the stylesheet alone, and its license), a stylesheet, and a script. During development, the [Django] server serves them itself ([django.contrib.staticfiles] application); in production, they are copied to [var/static] by the command [collectstatic], and served by the web server (“A production server”).

docs.title: 11.19.1. static/css/styles.css
docs.text:
/* =========================================================================
   static/css/styles.css - quelques réglages en plus de Bootstrap
   (les mêmes que dans les autres versions de cette application).
   ========================================================================= */

body {
  background-color: #f5f7fa;
}

.creneau-libre:hover {
  background-color: #e9f7ef;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   .zone-erreur : les messages d'erreur, en bas de page, sur fond rose léger
   (cf. templates/fragments/erreurs.html).
   position: sticky + bottom : si la page est plus haute que la fenêtre (un
   agenda de 12 créneaux, par exemple), la zone reste collée au bas de la
   fenêtre au lieu de disparaître sous la ligne de flottaison - sans jamais
   recouvrir le contenu quand la page est courte.
   z-index : au-dessus du fond grisé de la fenêtre de réservation (.modal-backdrop).
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
.zone-erreur {
  position: sticky;
  bottom: 1rem;
  z-index: 1060;
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  background-color: #fdecef; /* light pink */
  border: 1px solid #f5c2c7;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  color: #842029;
}

/* the two main options on the patient's "My Account" page */
.carte-option {
  transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s;
}

.carte-option:hover {
  border-color: #0d6efd;
  box-shadow: 0 0.25rem 0.75rem rgba(13, 110, 253, 0.15);
}

/* the CAPTCHA image (SVG, 150 x 50 pixels) */
.captcha-image svg {
  display: block;
  border: 1px solid #dee2e6;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
}

A few additional settings for [Bootstrap], the same as in the other versions of the application.

  • lines 10–12: a bookable slot in the calendar turns green on mouseover;
  • lines 23–33: the error area at the bottom of the page has a light pink background. [position: sticky] with [bottom: 1rem]: if the page is taller than the window (a calendar with 12 time slots), the area remains anchored to the bottom of the window instead of disappearing below the scroll bar; if the page is short, it stays in place without covering anything. [z-index]: It appears over the gray background of the booking window;
  • lines 36–43: the two large “My Account” cards, which light up when the mouse hovers over them;
  • lines 46–50: the CAPTCHA image, with a border.

docs.title: 11.19.2. static/js/app.js
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// static/js/app.js - the application's SEUL JavaScript.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The entire application works without JavaScript. This script adds a
// convenience feature: before submitting a form that includes the
// data-confirmation="...", a modal window asks "Are you sure?"
// (the window itself is located in the page: templates/fragments/confirmation.html).
// If JavaScript is disabled, the form simply submits without
// confirmation—nothing breaks (the principle of “progressive enhancement”).
//
// Why not window.confirm()? Its input field doesn’t format properly, and its
// buttons remain in the browser’s language, not the page’s.
// =========================================================================

(() => {
  const modale = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation');
  if (!modale) {
    return;
  }
  const message = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation-message');
  const boutonNon = modale.querySelector('.modal-footer [data-action="non"]');

  let formulaireEnAttente = null; // the form to submit if you confirm
  let focusPrecedent = null; // the element to focus on when closing

  function ouvrir(formulaire) {
    formulaireEnAttente = formulaire;
    focusPrecedent = document.activeElement;
     // textContent (not innerHTML): the message is displayed as TEXTE,
     // never interpreted as HTML
    message.textContent = formulaire.dataset.confirmation;
    modale.classList.remove('d-none');
     // the focus moves to "No": accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything
    boutonNon.focus();
  }

  function fermer() {
    modale.classList.add('d-none');
    formulaireEnAttente = null;
    if (focusPrecedent) {
      focusPrecedent.focus();
    }
  }

   // 1. Form submissions requiring confirmation are intercepted
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((formulaire) => {
    formulaire.addEventListener('submit', (evenement) => {
      evenement.preventDefault();
      ouvrir(formulaire);
    });
  });

   // 2. The window’s buttons (Yes / No / close button)
  modale.addEventListener('click', (evenement) => {
    const action = evenement.target.closest('[data-action]')?.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'oui') {
      const formulaire = formulaireEnAttente;
      fermer();
       // formulaire.submit() submits the form SANS to trigger again
       // The 'submit' event: no new confirmation request
      formulaire.submit();
    } else if (action === 'non') {
      fermer();
    } else if (evenement.target.classList.contains('modal')) {
      fermer(); // Click on the grayed-out background, outside the window
    }
  });

   // 3. Keyboard: Esc closes the window; Tab keeps the focus on the window
   /   / (otherwise, the focus would move to the grayed-out page behind it)
  modale.addEventListener('keydown', (evenement) => {
    if (evenement.key === 'Escape') {
      fermer();
    } else if (evenement.key === 'Tab') {
      const boutons = [...modale.querySelectorAll('button')];
      const premier = boutons[0];
      const dernier = boutons[boutons.length - 1];
      if (evenement.shiftKey && document.activeElement === premier) {
        evenement.preventDefault();
        dernier.focus();
      } else if (!evenement.shiftKey && document.activeElement === dernier) {
        evenement.preventDefault();
        premier.focus();
      }
    }
  });
})();

The only [JavaScript] in the application—the one from Example 21—with a few additions. The entire application works without [JavaScript]: this script adds convenience by providing a confirmation before submitting a form that carries the [data-confirmation] attribute. If [JavaScript] is disabled, the form submits without confirmation: nothing breaks (principle of progressive enhancement).

  • Lines 15–19: The script is a function called as soon as it is defined ([(() => { ... })()]); its variables are not visible to the rest of the page. Without a confirmation window on the page, it does nothing;
  • Lines 26–35: Opening the window: the form to be submitted if the user confirms is stored, and the form’s message is displayed in the window. [textContent], not [innerHTML]: the message is displayed as text and is never interpreted as HTML. Focus moves to the “No” button: accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything;
  • lines 37–43: closing the window; focus returns to the element that had it previously;
  • lines 46–51: the submission of each form to be confirmed is intercepted ([preventDefault] prevents it), and the window opens. The [submit] event occurs only after the browser’s validations: the current password, which is required ([required]) in the account deletion form, is required before the prompt;
  • lines 54–67: the buttons in the window. A single handler for the entire window: [closest('[data-action]')] finds the clicked button or the element containing it; [?.] ensures [undefined] returns no error if none match. “Yes” submits the form via [formulaire.submit()], which does not trigger the [submit] event: no new confirmation prompt appears. Clicking on the grayed-out background outside the window closes it;
  • lines 71–86: the keyboard. Esc closes the window; the Tab key moves the focus from one button to another without leaving the window (otherwise, it would move to the grayed-out page behind it): this is what users who navigate with the keyboard and screen readers expect.

docs.title: 12. Conclusion
docs.text:
This document described the development of a MVC web application using the [Django] framework: an application whose HTML pages are generated by the server using [Django] templates, without a browser-side [JavaScript] framework. He followed the [Symfony] course step by step, which itself builds upon the courses [Laravel], [Flask], [Spring MVC], [ASP.NET Core MVC], and [NestJS]: views and routing to templates, forms, internationalization, security, and data access, followed by a comprehensive case study.

The same 28 examples and the same application were thus written using seven frameworks: in [TypeScript], in [C#], in [Java], twice in [PHP], and twice in [Python]. The concepts are the same; only the names and mechanisms differ. The correspondences between [Symfony] and [Django]:

[Symfony][Django]core ([src/Kernel.php]), bundles, service container, dependency injectionsettings ([config/settings.py]), applications ([INSTALLED_APPS]), imported modules, providers ([functools.cache])[composer.json], folder [vendor], [php bin/console][requirements.txt], virtual environment ([.venv]), [python manage.py]file [.env], folder [config/packages] (files YAML), [%env(...)%]file [config/settings.py] (from [Python]), environment variables ([os.environ]), file [.env] read by us[#[Route]] attributes of the controllerslists [urlpatterns] ([path], [re_path], [include]), named routes, [app_name][render], [redirectToRoute], [generateUrl]; [path] in the views[render], [redirect], [reverse]; [{% url %}] in the templatesobject [Request], [requirements] ([{id<\d+>}]), argument resolvers, [#[MapQueryString]]object [HttpRequest] ([GET], [POST], [headers], [COOKIES]), converters ([<int:id>]), forms as validatorsValidator component (attribute constraints), Form component (types, [handleRequest], [isValid])[django.forms] forms (fields, validators, [clean], [error_messages], [is_valid], [cleaned_data])form theme [Bootstrap] 5rendering engine ([FORM_RENDERER]), field template, [as_field_group]views [Twig], [{{ }}], [{% for %}], [{% if %}]Templates for DTL, [{{ }}], [{% for %}] ... [{% empty %}], [{% if %}][{% extends %}] and blocks, [{% include %}], macros[{% extends %}] and blocks, [{% include %}], named fragments ([{% partialdef %}])global variables, extensions [Twig] (functions, filters)context processors, tag libraries ([templatetags]: filters, simple tags, inclusion tags)flash messages ([addFlash], [app.flashes]), file-based sessions[messages] application (signed cookie), sessions (files, signed cookie, database...)kernel event listeners ([kernel.request], [kernel.controller], [kernel.response]...)middleware ([__call__], [process_view], [process_exception]), signals ([request_started], [request_finished])headphones: [kernel.exception], [HttpException], [createNotFoundException][Http404], [PermissionDenied], [BadRequest], views [handler404]..., [process_exception]firewalls, authenticators, [access_control], [#[IsGranted]], votersauthentication and access control middleware written by us, decorators; or the [django.contrib.auth] applicationanti-CSRF token for the Form component, [csrf_token()], [isCsrfTokenValid][CsrfViewMiddleware] middleware, [{% csrf_token %}] tag, [CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW] (403 response, or 419 in our application)component [RateLimiter]a limiter written to the cacheFile [translations] (YAML, ICU), filter [trans], [TranslatorInterface]file [locale] ([gettext]: [.po], [.mo]), [gettext], [gettext_lazy], [ngettext], [{% translate %}], [{% blocktranslate %}][intl] extension: [IntlDateFormatter], [NumberFormatter]Formatting based on the active language (filter [date], [floatformat]), [Babel]Cache component (PSR-6 and contracts), Lock componentcache for [Django] ([LocMemCache], [FileBasedCache]...), [get_or_set][Doctrine]: Data Mapper entities, entity manager, DQL, and QueryBuilderORM from [Django]: Active Record models, managers ([objects]), [QuerySet], [select_related], [F()][wrapInTransaction(...)], [flush][transaction.atomic()], [select_for_update()][#[ORM\Version]], managed by [Doctrine] ([OptimisticLockException])[update()], version-dependent ([filter(version=...)]), written to the DAO layer[php -S localhost:8000 -t public], or [symfony server:start][python manage.py runserver]

Regarding [Symfony], the key points to note are:

  • the [Django] application is loaded once, when the server starts up, then remains in memory and processes all requests (example 01): the objects created at startup (settings, routes, middleware, services) are shared by all requests. It’s simple and fast, but it requires distinguishing between what belongs to the application (shared, and therefore without state specific to a request) and what belongs to a request (the [request] object, the local variables of the views), and to remember that a production server runs multiple processes, which share only what is stored outside of them (the database, the file cache);
  • no service container: services are [Python] modules that are imported, and provider functions that create a unique object on the first request. A module’s dependencies are visible in its [import] files; replacing them for testing purposes is done via a setting (example 06);
  • The configuration is a [Python] or [config/settings.py] file: a sequence of assignments that can be calculated, commented on, or split up. The [python manage.py diffsettings] command displays what differs from the default values;
  • The processing of a request passes through a list of middleware components in the order specified in the [MIDDLEWARE] list, and then in reverse order for the response: this is where language settings, anti-CSRF protection, authentication, access control, and error pages are handled. The mechanism is simpler than the kernel events in [Symfony]: the order of the list is the order of execution;
  • Views are simple functions that receive a request and return a response; decorators ([@require_POST], [@passe_inscription_exige]) wrap them to add control. We have written several of them, and even a class whose methods are views ([GestionPersonnes]), without requiring anything specific from [Django];
  • Forms are objects, described by classes: fields, value conversion, validators, input redisply, and error messages. They are rendered using templates that can be replaced (a rendering engine, a field template): fields throughout the application are rendered in the same way, using the classes from [Bootstrap] and accessibility attributes;
  • [Django] comes “ready to use”: sessions, messages, translations, cache, anti-CSRF protection, static files, ORM—everything is included, documented in one place, with no additional installation required. We’ve added only three libraries: the [MySQL] driver, [PyJWT], and [bcrypt]. The very comprehensive [django.contrib.auth] authentication application was left out: the case study database has its own users, and we wanted JWT tokens, just like the other versions of the application. Writing the authentication code from scratch, in about a hundred lines, demonstrated exactly what it does;
  • the ORM from [Django] follows the Active Record pattern: a model is a class linked to a table, where each object knows how to save itself. More straightforward than the Data Mapper in [Doctrine], it also works very well with an existing database ([managed = False], where table and column names are predefined). Its lazy [QuerySet], [select_related], [F()] expressions, and the conditional [update()] statements allow you to write efficient and safe queries, and the development mode console displays every SQL command sent to the database;
  • DTL templates use a deliberately limited language: no arithmetic, no function calls with parameters. A template can only display the data provided to it: this is both a constraint and a guarantee that drives logic into views and view models. Any missing information is added via filters and tags written in [Python]. Templates automatically escape whatever they display.

The case study shows that a classic HTML application, without the essential [JavaScript], remains a simple and robust solution: each page is a URL, the browser’s “Back” button works, and the server controls everything. The minimal use of [JavaScript] (confirmation windows) enhances the user experience without being necessary for functionality. [Django] can also support more interactive applications without straying from its templates (using the [htmx] library, for example, the named fragments from [Django] 6 work very well) or with a browser-side [JavaScript] framework, to which it provides a API JSON ([Django REST framework], [Django Ninja]): this will be covered in other documents.

For further information, please refer to the documentation for [Django] (docs.djangoproject.com, translated into French), particularly the pages dedicated to views and URL, forms, templates, middleware, internationalization, ORM, and security, its tutorial (which covers the administration interface and migrations, which are not covered here), the [Python] tutorial (docs.python.org/fr), and compare this application to its sister applications [Symfony], [Laravel], [Flask], [Spring MVC], [ASP.NET Core MVC], and [NestJS].

docs.title: 6. Data Scopes
docs.text:
A web application serves many users at once, and each user makes numerous requests. Data can therefore be shared at several levels, known as its scope:

  • application scope: the data is shared by all users throughout the application’s lifetime (the list of doctors, for example);
  • request scope: the data exists only for the duration of a request (a template’s model, the logged-in user as identified for that request);
  • session scope: the data is specific to a user and must persist from one request to the next (the selected language, a shopping cart);
  • client scope: data stored in the browser itself, in a cookie.

In [Python], these scopes take on a different nature than what readers of the [Symfony] course are familiar with, because the application remains in memory from one request to the next (Example 01). Data stored in a module variable (examples 06, 20, and 21) naturally has application scope: this is convenient and very fast. But this scope has two limitations. First, it lasts only for the duration of the process: a server restart clears it. Second, it is process-specific: in production, multiple application processes are typically launched (several “workers” of [gunicorn], for example), or even multiple servers behind a load balancer, and each would have its own copy of the data. Data that truly needs to be shared and persist over time is therefore stored in a database or in a shared cache ([Redis], [Memcached], which [Django] knows how to use via its [CACHES] setting). In exchange for speed, sharing requires strict discipline: a process handles multiple requests at once, across multiple threads, and shared data modified by one process is visible to all; it must be protected by a lock (example 20), and data belonging to a specific user must never be stored there.

In [Django], each scope has its own container:

ScopeContainerLifetimeapplicationa module variable (a single process), the [Django] cache ([CACHES] setting), or the databasethe one for the process; the duration selected for the cache; no limit for the databasequerythe [HttpRequest] object, to which a middleware component can add attributes (Example 12); the view’s local variablesthe processing of a querysessionthe session ([request.session], application [django.contrib.sessions]), maintained by the server, retrieved via a cookietwo weeks by default (setting [SESSION_COOKIE_AGE])clienta cookie ([set_cookie], example 22), either in plain text or signed ([set_signed_cookie])the cookie’s specified duration

The session for [Django] is, by default, a server-side session, like those for [Java] ([JSESSIONID]) or [PHP] ([PHPSESSID]): its data is stored on the server, and the browser only holds the identifier—a random number that is impossible to guess—in the [sessionid] cookie. The [SESSION_ENGINE] setting determines where the data is stored: in the database (the default option, in a table named [django_session]), in the cache, in files (the option used in our example), or even, as in the case of [Flask], entirely in a signed cookie on the client’s device.

docs.title: 6.1.2. The objects: scores/compteurs.py and scores/middleware.py
docs.text:
# scopes/compteurs.py: scope APPLICATION, counters shared by all
# requests from all users

import threading
from collections import Counter

# a Counter: a dictionary {key: number}, where missing keys are set to 0. It is
# created when the module loads, and lives as long as the server process
_compteurs = Counter()
_verrou = threading.Lock()


# an additional number under the key [cle]; += is not an atomic operation: two
# concurrent requests could read the same value. The lock prevents this
def suivant(cle: str) -> int:
    with _verrou:
        _compteurs[cle] += 1
        return _compteurs[cle]
  • Line 5: the class [Counter] from the module [collections]: a dictionary whose values are numbers, and whose missing keys are set to 0;
  • Lines 9–10: the counters and their lock, created when the module is loaded; they exist for as long as the server process runs. This is the application scope;
  • lines 15–18: one more number under a key. The operation [+=] is not atomic: it reads the value, increments it, then writes it, and two simultaneous requests could read the same value—a visit would be lost. The lock (example 20) prevents this.
# scopes/middleware.py: scope REQUÊTE, information from a request

from dataclasses import dataclass

from django.utils import timezone

from . import compteurs


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RequeteInfos:
    numero: int
    debut: str


# the middleware creates UN object RequeteInfos per request, and stores it in the request:
# The view and template retrieve it via request.infos. It disappears along with the view and template
class InfosRequete:
    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):
        request.infos = RequeteInfos(
             # a number created via OBJET, drawn from a counter shared by all requests
            numero=compteurs.suivant("instances"),
             # the time, including milliseconds
            debut=timezone.localtime().strftime("%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3])
        return self.get_response(request)
  • lines 10–13: request scope information: a number and the request time;
  • lines 18–28: the middleware creates a [RequeteInfos] object for each request and stores it in the request (Example 12). The number is taken from a counter shared by all requests (the previous module, under a different key); therefore, each object has a different number. The time is written including milliseconds: [%f] represents the microseconds (six digits), from which [[:-3]] removes the last three (a string slice: all characters except the last three). The object is deleted along with the request.

[Django] has no service container, and therefore no “request-scope service”: it is the request itself that carries the objects in this scope. Readers of the [Symfony] course will recall that it was the opposite: in [PHP], every service was request-scoped, and a cache was required to obtain application scope.

docs.title: 6.1.3. Signed Cookies
docs.text:
A cookie is a piece of data entrusted to the client, which can read and modify it. For a cookie to be trustworthy, it simply needs to be signed: its value travels in plaintext, but it is followed by a signature that only the server knows how to calculate, because it depends on a secret key. A value modified by the client no longer has the correct signature, and the server rejects it. [Django] handles this for us: [reponse.set_signed_cookie(nom, valeur)] sets a signed cookie, and [request.get_signed_cookie(nom, default=...)] returns its value if the signature is correct; otherwise, it returns the default value. The signature is a HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code): a hash of the value (SHA-256), calculated using the application’s secret key ([SECRET_KEY], example 01), and a “salt” specific to the cookie’s name. [Django] adds the signature date, which allows an outdated cookie to be rejected ([get_signed_cookie(..., max_age=3600)]). The verification process compares the signatures in a time that does not depend on the number of identical characters: a standard comparison would stop at the first differing character, and an attacker could, by measuring the response time, guess the signature character by character. The [django.core.signing] module offers the same functions for signing any data ([signing.dumps], [signing.loads]): it is this module that signs the flash messages in Example 20.

This is the principle behind the JWT token, which the next chapter will use for authentication.

docs.title: 6.1.4. The view: scopes/views.py
docs.text:
# ranges/views.py: the four data ranges

from django.shortcuts import render
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET

from . import compteurs


@require_GET
def portees(request):
     # APPLICATION: the shared counter
    total = compteurs.suivant("visites")
     # SESSION: browser-specific data, stored in CE (a
     # var/sessions file), retrieved via the session cookie; the session
     # is used as a dictionary
    request.session["visites"] = request.session.get("visites", 0) + 1
     # CLIENT: data stored by NAVIGATEUR in cookies, sent back to the
     # server with each request; one in plain text, the other signed
    mes_visites = int(request.COOKIES.get("mesVisites", 0)) + 1
     # get_signed_cookie: the value if the signature is valid; default otherwise
    mes_visites_signe = int(request.get_signed_cookie("mesVisitesSigne", default=0)) + 1
    reponse = render(request, "portees/portees.html", {
        "total": total,
        "instance": request.infos.numero,
        "visites_session": request.session["visites"],
        "mes_visites": mes_visites,
        "mes_visites_signe": mes_visites_signe,
    })
    reponse.set_cookie("mesVisites", str(mes_visites))
     # set_signed_cookie: the value, followed by a signature calculated using SECRET_KEY
    reponse.set_signed_cookie("mesVisitesSigne", str(mes_visites_signe))
    return reponse
  • line 12: the application scope;
  • line 16: the session scope. [request.session] is used like a dictionary: [get(clé, défaut)] reads a value, and the assignment writes it. [Django] saves the session at the end of the request. Values must be convertible to JSON (strings, numbers, lists, dictionaries): this is how they are stored;
  • Lines 19–21: the client scope, with two cookies. [request.COOKIES] is the dictionary of cookies sent by the browser. Their values are strings provided by the browser and may therefore be missing or invalid: [int] converts them (a cookie named [mesVisites=abc] would throw a [ValueError] exception here and result in a 500 error; a real application would verify the value; see example 07). The value of the signed cookie is accepted only if its signature is correct;
  • lines 22–28: the template context;
  • lines 29–31: To set a cookie, you need the response object: [render] constructs it (example 13), then [set_cookie] and [set_signed_cookie] add the cookies to it. Without an expiration time ([max_age]), a cookie lasts until the browser is closed (this is a “session” cookie, as defined by browsers).

docs.title: 6.1.6. Execution
docs.text:
After three visits in a browser:

The request object number is greater than the number of visits: on the first visit, the browser also requested the site icon ([/favicon.ico]), which does not exist. This request, which resulted in a 404 error, passed through the middleware and therefore had its own object, [RequeteInfos].

Let’s track the requests with [curl], which acts as a first browser by storing its cookies in the file [a.txt] (the server has just been started):

curl -i -c a.txt -b a.txt http://localhost:8000/

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Vary: Cookie
Set-Cookie: mesVisites=1; Path=/
Set-Cookie: mesVisitesSigne=1:1xAspS:4Nvkcx3peL8C64QPSFZNbB4KciM5Vv3OCuAR9bEMZwc; Path=/
Set-Cookie: sessionid=up3xpr7qnr8gj95hw4w0v1a1v4wnow79; expires=Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:38:22 GMT; HttpOnly; Max-Age=1209600; Path=/; SameSite=Lax
...
      <li>application : 1 visite(s) du site, tous navigateurs confondus</li>
      <li>requête : objet n° 1 (n° 1 dans le gabarit),
        requête reçue à 19:38:22.950</li>
      <li>session : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur (1 dans le gabarit)</li>
      <li>client : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur (cookie en clair),
        1 (cookie signé)</li>
...

The response sets three cookies. The first, [mesVisites], contains the value in plain text. The second, [mesVisitesSigne], contains the same value, followed by a colon, the signature date (in base 62), and the signature itself. The third, [sessionid], is the session ID, valid for two weeks ([Max-Age=1209600] seconds), [HttpOnly], and [SameSite=Lax] (example 20). The session data is stored in a file on the server, [var/sessions/sessionidup3xpr7qnr8gj95hw4w0v1a1v4wnow79], whose name is derived from the identifier:

eyJ2aXNpdGVzIjoxfQ:1xAspS:kBLb-izAURiIYXcjkHm2aDLFw8Vdgbm_Jxpq0f0ErA4

Here we can recognize the format of the signed data from [Django]: the data, the date, and the signature. The data is from JSON, encoded in Base64: [eyJ2aXNpdGVzIjoxfQ] decodes to [{"visites":1}]. The server even signs its own session files: a file modified by a third party would be rejected. A second visit, with the same cookies:

curl -i -c a.txt -b a.txt http://localhost:8000/

...
Set-Cookie: mesVisites=2; Path=/
Set-Cookie: mesVisitesSigne=2:1xAspS:pxWJZHoXRsALnFoTXbCOEfmTMgpOG0VtI-cosaBWPWo; Path=/
Set-Cookie: sessionid=up3xpr7qnr8gj95hw4w0v1a1v4wnow79; expires=Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:38:22 GMT; HttpOnly; Max-Age=1209600; Path=/; SameSite=Lax
...
      <li>application : 2 visite(s) du site, tous navigateurs confondus</li>
      <li>requête : objet n° 2 (n° 2 dans le gabarit),
        requête reçue à 19:38:22.972</li>
      <li>session : 2 visite(s) de ce navigateur (2 dans le gabarit)</li>
      <li>client : 2 visite(s) de ce navigateur (cookie en clair),
        2 (cookie signé)</li>
...

The session is the same (same ID); its cookie is sent back because the session has been modified, which extends its lifetime. A second “browser,” with its own cookie file, initially empty:

curl -c b.txt -b b.txt http://localhost:8000/

      <li>application : 3 visite(s) du site, tous navigateurs confondus</li>
      <li>requête : objet n° 3 (n° 3 dans le gabarit),
        requête reçue à 19:38:22.987</li>
      <li>session : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur (1 dans le gabarit)</li>
      <li>client : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur (cookie en clair),
        1 (cookie signé)</li>

The application counter has continued; the session and cookies for the second browser start over at 1. Each request had its own [RequeteInfos] object, and in each one, the view and template were the same. Finally, a malicious user forges their own cookies: 1,000 visits in [mesVisites], 999 in [mesVisitesSigne] (with a fabricated signature), and a session ID of their own invention:

curl -i -b "mesVisites=1000;mesVisitesSigne=999:abc;sessionid=abc" http://localhost:8000/

...
Set-Cookie: mesVisites=1001; Path=/
Set-Cookie: mesVisitesSigne=1:1xAspT:L8gY1VsFmTmnExyPBzfi-PIKW2S4uEJ_N5BlNbKA7M0; Path=/
Set-Cookie: sessionid=fd7i64x53xvaq1d4vpcxqj74kai4s9n7; expires=Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:38:23 GMT; HttpOnly; Max-Age=1209600; Path=/; SameSite=Lax
...
      <li>session : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur (1 dans le gabarit)</li>
      <li>client : 1001 visite(s) de ce navigateur (cookie en clair),
        1 (cookie signé)</li>
...

The plaintext cookie was accepted as-is: 1,001 visits. The cookie [mesVisitesSigne], however, did not have the correct signature: it was ignored, as if it were missing. Copying the signature from another value (that of [1], for example, next to the value [999]) doesn’t work any better: the signature depends on the value. As for the made-up session ID, it does not refer to any existing session: [Django] ignores it and creates a new session with a new ID that it chooses itself. The user therefore cannot select another user’s session.

Let’s remember the rule: data coming from the client is trustworthy only if it is protected by the server (signed, as here or as with the token in the chapter on authentication, or encrypted); data that has nothing to hide, and whose value is verified by the server (the language in Example 22), can remain in plaintext. A signature guarantees that a value has not been altered, but it does not hide it: a secret must never be entrusted to the client, even if it is signed.

The case study brings them together into a complete, realistic-sized application (nearly 90 files, approximately 5,500 lines, including comments). It was written with the same care as the examples: each file begins with a comment explaining its role, and tricky sections are annotated in the code. Each main folder also contains a file named [README.md] that lists its files. The document’s comments highlight what the examples did not show and refer to them for the rest.

docs.title: 5. Internationalization
docs.text:
An internationalized application displays its text in the user’s language. The case study is in French and English. The principle is simple: the templates contain text marked as “to be translated,” and a dictionary for each language associates each text with its translation. The selected language is stored in a cookie.

[Django] uses [gettext] for this purpose, the translation system from the GNU project, which [Python] also recognizes (the [gettext] module from the standard library), and which is found in many open-source software programs. With [gettext], the key for a text is the text itself, written in the original language: a template written in [{% translate "Accueil" %}], and the English dictionary associates “Accueil” with “Home.” A page thus remains readable and functional even without a dictionary: the text is displayed in the original language. This differs from versions [Symfony], [Laravel], [Flask], [Spring MVC], [ASP.NET Core MVC], and [NestJS] from the case study, which used abstract keys ([MENU.ACCUEIL]). Dictionaries are text files in the [.po] (Portable Object) format, which tools can extract from the code and which translation software can edit; [Django] reads their compiled version, the [.mo] (Machine Object) files. [gettext] can also inflect text into the plural form according to the rules of each language. [Django] is itself translated in this way: it is thanks to its dictionaries that its error messages have been in French since Example 08. The formatting of dates and amounts remains the same as in Example 16.
